docs.t: Montana anti-SLAPP — Procedure: 60 days to file, automatic stay, 60-day hearing and ruling
docs.x: Montana anti-SLAPP. Procedure: 60 days to file, automatic stay, 60-day hearing and ruling: File a special motion for expedited relief within 60 days after being served with the complaint, counterclaim, crossclaim, third-party complaint, or other pleading, or later for good cause. Filing stays all other proceedings between the movant and the responding party, including discovery and pending motions, until the ruling and the time to appeal run out; on motion the court may also stay related matters with other parties. Limited discovery is allowed only if specific information is needed to meet a burden and is not otherwise reasonably available. The court must hear the motion within 60 days after filing (later for allowed discovery or good cause) and rule within 60 days after the hearing. Not stayed: fee motions, voluntary dismissal or severance, and, for good cause, unrelated motions and pub

docs.t: Montana anti-SLAPP — Standard: dismissal with prejudice
docs.x: Montana anti-SLAPP. Standard: dismissal with prejudice: The court looks at the pleadings, the motion papers, and any evidence usable on summary judgment under M. R. Civ. P. 56. It must dismiss with prejudice if the movant shows the Act applies, the responding party fails to show an exclusion, and either the responding party fails to make a prima facie case on each essential element, or the movant shows failure to state a claim or no genuine issue of material fact. A voluntary dismissal without prejudice does not defeat the movant’s right to a ruling and fees; a voluntary dismissal with prejudice makes the movant the prevailing party. (Mont. Code Ann. 27-34-106, -107)

docs.t: Montana anti-SLAPP — Fees: mandatory for a winning movant
docs.x: Montana anti-SLAPP. Fees: mandatory for a winning movant: The court must award costs, reasonable attorney fees, and reasonable litigation expenses related to the motion to a movant who prevails. A responding party gets them only if it prevails and the court finds the motion frivolous or filed solely to delay. (Mont. Code Ann. 27-34-110)

docs.t: Montana anti-SLAPP — Appeal: of right, on a Montana-specific clock
docs.x: Montana anti-SLAPP. Appeal: of right, on a Montana-specific clock: A movant may appeal as of right from an order denying the motion in whole or part. The statute sets its own deadline: 30 days after entry of the order between private parties, 60 days if the United States, the State, or a political subdivision is a party. An appeal stays all proceedings between all parties until it ends (subject to the same exceptions). (Mont. Code Ann. 27-34-109, -104(3))

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (civil, private parties)
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (civil, private parties): 30 days from Entry of judgment or order (or service of notice of entry where M. R. Civ. P. 77(d) requires it) (M. R. App. P. 4(5)(a)(i)). Filed with the Clerk of the Supreme Court with the fee; jurisdictional (out-of-time appeal only under Rule 4(6)).

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (government party)
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (government party): 60 days from Entry of judgment or order (or service of notice of entry) (M. R. App. P. 4(5)(a)(i)). When the U.S., Montana, a political subdivision, or an officer or agency is a party (except abuse-and-neglect cases, which are 30 days).

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Notice of cross-appeal
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Notice of cross-appeal: 15 days from Filing of the first notice of appeal (or the regular appeal time, if later) (M. R. App. P. 4(5)(a)(iv)). Whichever period ends last.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Notice of entry of judgment (served by prevailing party)
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Notice of entry of judgment (served by prevailing party): 14 days from Entry of judgment or order (M. R. Civ. P. 77(d)). Where required, the appeal time does not run until it is served.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Rule 50(b), 52(b), 59 motions
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Rule 50(b), 52(b), 59 motions: 28 days from Entry of judgment (M. R. Civ. P. 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e), 6(b)(2)). Cannot be extended. Restart the appeal time.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Ruling on post-judgment motion, or deemed denied
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Ruling on post-judgment motion, or deemed denied: 60 days from Filing of the motion (M. R. Civ. P. 59(f); M. R. App. P. 4(5)(a)(v)). Extendable by order within 60 days, but deemed denied at 120 days. Appeal time runs from the deemed denial.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Attorney fee motion
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Attorney fee motion: 14 days from Entry of judgment (M. R. Civ. P. 54(d)(2)(B)(i)). Unless a statute or order provides otherwise; judgment is not appealable until the amount is fixed.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Amended notice after clerk’s deficiency notice
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Amended notice after clerk’s deficiency notice: 11 days from Clerk’s notice (M. R. App. P. 4(4)(e)).

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Notice of constitutional challenge (State not a party)
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Notice of constitutional challenge (State not a party): 11 days from Filing of the notice of appeal or cross-appeal (M. R. App. P. 27). To the Supreme Court and the Attorney General.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Select appellate mediator (Rule 7 cases)
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Select appellate mediator (Rule 7 cases): 15 days from Filing of the notice of appeal or triggering cross-appeal (M. R. App. P. 7(4)(b)–(c)). Otherwise the clerk appoints; 75 days to complete mediation.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Appellee’s additional transcript order
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Appellee’s additional transcript order: 11 days from Filing of the notice of appeal or cross-appeal, whichever is later (M. R. App. P. 8(3)(b)). Appellant orders transcripts the same day it files the notice.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Transmission of the record
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Transmission of the record: 40 days from Filing of the notice of appeal (or cross-appeal) (M. R. App. P. 9(1)). District court may extend to no more than 90 days from the first notice; further extensions only from the Supreme Court.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Appellant’s opening brief
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Appellant’s opening brief: 30 days from Filing of the record (M. R. App. P. 13(1)). One 30-day extension available; later ones presumptively denied.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Appellee’s answer brief
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Appellee’s answer brief: 30 days from Service of the opening brief (M. R. App. P. 13(1)).

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Reply brief: 14 days from Service of the answer brief (M. R. App. P. 13(1)). Combined reply and cross-answer: 30 days after the cross-appellant’s brief.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Response to a motion
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Response to a motion: 11 days from Service of the motion (M. R. App. P. 16(2)). No reply allowed.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Motion in Supreme Court for stay relief
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Motion in Supreme Court for stay relief: 11 days from Entry of the district court’s stay order (M. R. App. P. 22(2)(a)). Response within 11 days of filing.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Petition for rehearing
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Petition for rehearing: 15 days from Filing of the Supreme Court’s decision (M. R. App. P. 20(2)(a)). Objections 15 days after the petition; extension of at most 15 days.

docs.t: Montana appeal deadline — Appeal from denial of anti-SLAPP motion
docs.x: Montana appellate deadline. Appeal from denial of anti-SLAPP motion: 30 days from Entry of the order (Mont. Code Ann. 27-34-109). 60 days if the U.S., the State, or a political subdivision is a party.

docs.t: North Carolina — Serve within 60 days or keep the summons chain alive
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Serve within 60 days or keep the summons chain alive: Personal service must be made within 60 days after the summons issues. To keep the case alive against an unserved defendant, get an endorsement or an alias or pluries summons within 90 days of the last one. If the chain breaks, the action is discontinued as to that defendant and, if revived, counts as commenced only on the new date. That can blow the statute of limitations. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 4(c)–(e))

docs.t: North Carolina — Do not plead a dollar figure in negligence or punitive claims
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Do not plead a dollar figure in negligence or punitive claims: In negligence actions and punitive damage claims over $25,000, the complaint must say only that damages exceed $25,000. The defendant may demand a written statement of the amount, due within 30 days. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 8(a)(2))

docs.t: North Carolina — Jury demand: 10 days after the last pleading
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Jury demand: 10 days after the last pleading: Serve and file a written jury demand within 10 days after service of the last pleading on the issue (federal: 14). Missing it waives the jury. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 38(b), (d))

docs.t: North Carolina — Post-trial motions in 10 days, no extensions
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Post-trial motions in 10 days, no extensions: JNOV, motions to amend findings, and new-trial or alter-or-amend motions are due 10 days after entry of judgment (federal: 28). Neither the court nor a stipulation can extend these deadlines. The usual 30-day stipulated extension under Rule 6(b) does not apply. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 6(b), 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e))

docs.t: North Carolina — Requests for admission can come with the summons
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Requests for admission can come with the summons: A plaintiff may serve requests for admission with the summons and complaint. They are deemed admitted unless answered within 30 days after service, except that a defendant gets at least 60 days from service of the summons. Deemed admissions are conclusive unless withdrawn on motion. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 36(a), (b); 4(b))

docs.t: North Carolina — Voluntary dismissal: easy once, fatal twice, one-year refiling
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Voluntary dismissal: easy once, fatal twice, one-year refiling: A plaintiff can dismiss by notice any time before resting. A second notice dismissal of the same claim is an adjudication on the merits. A timely action dismissed without prejudice may be refiled within one year, but the refiled case is stayed until costs from the first case are paid. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 41(a)(1), (d))

docs.t: North Carolina — Pro hac vice needs out-of-state domicile, reciprocity and a resident co-counsel
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Pro hac vice needs out-of-state domicile, reciprocity and a resident co-counsel: Only an attorney domiciled in another state qualifies. The motion must state that the home state grants like privileges to North Carolina lawyers and that a North Carolina resident attorney is associated and personally appearing. It must include a client-signed retention statement and the $225 fee. The court keeps discretion and may revoke summarily. (N.C.G.S. §§ 84-4.1, 84-4.2)

docs.t: North Carolina — Business Court designation: 30 days, and waiver
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Business Court designation: 30 days, and waiver: A defendant who wants Business Court must file the Notice of Designation within 30 days after receiving service of the pleading. A party opposing designation has 30 days after service of the notice and waives any ground not asserted. (N.C.G.S. § 7A-45.4(d)(3), (e))

docs.t: North Carolina — Appeal to the right court
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Appeal to the right court: Final judgments in designated business cases, interlocutory Business Court orders affecting a substantial right, and every Rule 23 class-certification ruling are appealed directly to the Supreme Court, not the Court of Appeals. (N.C.G.S. § 7A-27(a)(2)–(4))

docs.t: North Carolina — A Court of Appeals dissent no longer gets you to the Supreme Court
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. A Court of Appeals dissent no longer gets you to the Supreme Court: The appeal of right based on a dissent was repealed effective July 1, 2023. Without a substantial constitutional question, further review requires a petition for discretionary review. (N.C.G.S. §§ 7A-30, 7A-31)

docs.t: North Carolina — Rule 9(j) certification in medical malpractice
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Rule 9(j) certification in medical malpractice: A malpractice complaint is dismissed unless it asserts that an expert reasonably expected to qualify under Rule 702 reviewed the care and records and will testify that the standard was breached, or it pleads res ipsa loquitur. A 120-day limitations extension is available only by motion before the statute runs. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 9(j))

docs.t: North Carolina — Rule 11 sanctions are mandatory, with no safe harbor
docs.x: North Carolina land mine. Rule 11 sanctions are mandatory, with no safe harbor: If a paper is signed in violation of Rule 11, the court ‘shall impose’ an appropriate sanction on the signer, the party, or both. The text has no 21-day withdrawal window like the federal rule. (N.C. R. Civ. P. 11(a))

docs.t: North Carolina anti-SLAPP — No anti-SLAPP statute
docs.x: North Carolina anti-SLAPP. No anti-SLAPP statute: North Carolina has no anti-SLAPP law: no special motion to dismiss, no discovery stay, and no speech-based fee-shifting. docs.t: North Carolina appeal deadline — Serve signed judgment on all parties
docs.x: North Carolina appellate deadline. Serve signed judgment on all parties: 3 days from Entry of judgment (written, signed, filed) (N.C. R. Civ. P. 58). Failure tolls Rule 50(b), 52(b) and 59 periods, but not beyond 90 days from entry.

docs.t: North Carolina appeal deadline — JNOV, motion to amend findings, new-trial or alter/amend motion
docs.x: North Carolina appellate deadline. JNOV, motion to amend findings, new-trial or alter/amend motion: 10 days from Entry of judgment (N.C. R. Civ. P. 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e)). Cannot be extended by the court or by stipulation (Rule 6(b)). Add 3 days if the judgment was served by mail (Rule 58).

docs.t: North Carolina appeal deadline — Notice of appeal, civil case
docs.x: North Carolina appellate deadline. Notice of appeal, civil case: 30 days from Entry of judgment if served within 3 days under Rule 58; otherwise service of the judgment (N.C.G.S. § 1-279.1; N.C. R. App. P. 3(c)). Appellate-rule deadline NOT verified against collected text (nccourts.gov blocked). Tolled by a timely Rule 50(b), 52(b) or 59 motion under App. R. 3(c)(3).

docs.t: North Carolina appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (G.S. 7A-30) or petition for discretionary review to the Supreme Court
docs.x: North Carolina appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (G.S. 7A-30) or petition for discretionary review to the Supreme Court: 15 days from Issuance of the Court of Appeals’ mandate (N.C.G.S. §§ 7A-30, 7A-31; N.C. R. App. P. 14, 15). Rules NOT verified; Rules 14–16 reportedly amended effective April 1, 2025. Dissent-based appeals of right were repealed July 1, 2023.

docs.t: North Carolina appeal deadline — Rule 60(b)(1)–(3) motion
docs.x: North Carolina appellate deadline. Rule 60(b)(1)–(3) motion: 365 days from Entry of the judgment or order (N.C. R. Civ. P. 60(b)). Does not toll the time to appeal or suspend the judgment.

docs.t: North Dakota — The case starts on service, and the defendant can force you to file in 20 days
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. The case starts on service, and the defendant can force you to file in 20 days: A civil action is commenced by service of the summons, not by filing. A defendant may serve a demand that the plaintiff file; if the complaint is not filed within 20 days after service of the demand, the service of the summons is void (relief only by motion within 60 days on excusable neglect). When you do file, proof of Rule 4 service must accompany the initiating pleading. (N.D.R.Civ.P. 3, 5(d)(2)(A))

docs.t: North Dakota — Appeal time runs 60 days from service of notice of entry, and the notice goes to the Supreme Court clerk
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Appeal time runs 60 days from service of notice of entry, and the notice goes to the Supreme Court clerk: File the notice of appeal with the clerk of the Supreme Court within 60 days from service of notice of entry of judgment, together with the transcript order. The prevailing party must serve notice of entry within 14 days. Do not wait for service if you have acted on the judgment: the record showing your own actual knowledge of entry can start the clock. An extension (up to 30 days) must be sought within 30 days after the deadline. (N.D.R.App.P. 3(a), 4(a)(1), (a)(4), 10(b)(1)(E); N.D.R.Civ.P. 58(b))

docs.t: North Dakota — Ten days to demand a new judge, and one ruling ends the right
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Ten days to demand a new judge, and one ruling ends the right: The no-cause demand for change of judge must be filed within 10 days after notice of the judge’s assignment for trial, notice of a trial date, or service of that judge’s ex parte order, whichever comes first. It is barred once the judge rules on any matter in which your client was heard or could have been heard, so even a routine motion hearing can forfeit it. The client must sign, or the attorney signs with permission and files a certificate of mailing a copy to the client. (N.D.C.C. § 29-15-21(1)-(4))

docs.t: North Dakota — Motion practice runs on briefs: 14 days to answer, and silence is an admission
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Motion practice runs on briefs: 14 days to answer, and silence is an admission: The movant serves and files a notice and brief; the opponent has 14 days after service to serve and file an answer brief, and the reply is due 7 days later. The motion is then decided on the briefs unless a party requests a hearing within 7 days after the answer-brief deadline, and the requester must secure a hearing time within 14 days or the request is waived. Failing to file an answer brief may be treated as an admission that the motion has merit. Extensions require a written order. (N.D.R.Ct. 3.2(a), (c), (d))

docs.t: North Dakota — Summary judgment has its own outer deadlines and page limits
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Summary judgment has its own outer deadlines and page limits: The motion and supporting papers must be filed at least 90 days before trial and 45 days before the hearing unless ordered otherwise. The response is due 30 days after service of the brief, and the reply 14 days later. Principal and answer briefs are limited to 38 pages, replies to 12 (footnotes included); a request to exceed must be filed at least 7 days before the brief is due. (N.D.R.Civ.P. 56(c)(1)-(2))

docs.t: North Dakota — Jury demand within 14 days, and you get six jurors unless you ask for nine
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Jury demand within 14 days, and you get six jurors unless you ask for nine: Serve a written jury demand no later than 14 days after the last pleading directed to the issue, and file it; otherwise the jury is waived. A civil jury has six members unless a party specifically demands nine within the same 14 days. Each side gets only four peremptory challenges regardless of the number of parties. (N.D.R.Civ.P. 38(b)-(c), (e), 47(c)(1), 48(b))

docs.t: North Dakota — Medical negligence: expert affidavit within three months of commencement
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Medical negligence: expert affidavit within three months of commencement: An action alleging professional negligence by a physician, nurse, hospital, licensed care facility, or other health care organization must be dismissed without prejudice on motion unless the plaintiff serves an affidavit with an admissible expert opinion supporting a prima facie case within three months after commencement. An extension requires good cause and a request made before the three months run. Obvious-occurrence cases (wrong patient or body part, retained foreign object) are excepted. (N.D.C.C. § 28-01-46)

docs.t: North Dakota — Plead frivolousness in the answer if you want mandatory fees
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Plead frivolousness in the answer if you want mandatory fees: The court must award the prevailing party costs and attorney’s fees for a frivolous claim, but only if the prevailing party alleged the claim’s frivolous nature in its responsive pleading. Leaving it out of the answer forfeits the mandatory award. (N.D.C.C. § 28-26-01(2))

docs.t: North Dakota — Pro hac vice: 45-day filing window and a five-case cap
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Pro hac vice: 45-day filing window and a five-case cap: The motion and affidavit must be filed no later than 45 days after service of the pleading, motion, or paper, with copies and the fee sent to the State Board of Law Examiners at the same time. More than five pro hac vice appearances within 12 months is presumed excessive. The North Dakota associate must appear with you at every appearance unless excused. (Admission to Practice R. 3(A)(1)-(4))

docs.t: North Dakota — Number every paragraph and cite the record by index number
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Number every paragraph and cite the record by index number: Every electronically filed trial-court document prepared by the parties must number its paragraphs, and references must be to paragraph numbers, not pages. On appeal, record citations must use the register-of-actions index format, for example (R156:12), and “Id.” may not be used for record citations. Briefs that do not comply will not be filed. (N.D.R.Ct. 3.5(b)(2); N.D.R.App.P. 30, 32(a)(7), (c))

docs.t: North Dakota — Post-trial motions run from notice of entry, and some cannot be extended
docs.x: North Dakota land mine. Post-trial motions run from notice of entry, and some cannot be extended: Renewed JMOL, amended findings, and motions to alter or amend are due 28 days after notice of entry of judgment, and the court cannot extend those times. A new-trial motion is due within 60 days (6 months for newly discovered evidence). Costs require a verified statement within 30 days after the order for judgment, and an attorney’s-fee motion is due 21 days after notice of entry. (N.D.R.Civ.P. 6(b)(2), 50(b), 52(b), 54(e), 59(c), (j))

docs.t: North Dakota anti-SLAPP — No anti-SLAPP statute found in the Century Code
docs.x: North Dakota anti-SLAPP. No anti-SLAPP statute found in the Century Code: A search of the Legislative Branch’s full Century Code section index (all titles, chapter and section headings) found no anti-SLAPP law, no Uniform Public Expression Protection Act, and no section on strategic lawsuits, public participation in litigation, or public expression. North Dakota therefore has no special motion to dismiss, discovery stay, or interlocutory appeal for speech-based suits. The check was of headings, not every section’s full text. (N.D.C.C. index (ndlegis.gov), checked November 10, 2026)

docs.t: North Dakota anti-SLAPP — Closest tools: mandatory fees for frivolous claims, and Rule 11
docs.x: North Dakota anti-SLAPP. Closest tools: mandatory fees for frivolous claims, and Rule 11: In civil actions the court must award reasonable actual and statutory costs, including attorney’s fees, to the prevailing party on finding a claim for relief frivolous: so completely lacking in facts or law that a reasonable person could not have expected to win. The prevailing party must have alleged the frivolous nature of the claim in its responsive pleading, so a defendant must plead it in the answer. A good-faith argument to extend, modify, or reverse the law is protected. A party pleading allegations or denials without reasonable cause and not in good faith, found untrue, pays the other side’s resulting expenses and fees. Rule 11 sanctions (with a 21-day safe harbor) and Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal are otherwise the ordinary routes. (N.D.C.C. §§ 28-26-01(2), 28-26-31; N.D.R.Civ.P. 11(c), 12(b)(6))

docs.t: North Dakota anti-SLAPP — Repeat litigants: statewide vexatious-litigant pre-filing orders
docs.x: North Dakota anti-SLAPP. Repeat litigants: statewide vexatious-litigant pre-filing orders: A presiding judge, on request or on the court’s own motion, may designate a vexatious litigant (for example, two adverse litigations involving vexatious conduct in seven years, repeated relitigation, or a prior designation by any court) and enter a pre-filing order requiring leave of court for new filings, possibly with security. The order must award the costs and reasonable attorney’s fees of responding, including the cost of obtaining the order. The litigant has 14 days to respond to the proposed order. A designation by a presiding judge is appealable. (N.D. Sup. Ct. Admin. R. 58, §§ 2-6)

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (civil)
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (civil): 60 days from Service of notice of entry of the judgment or order (N.D.R.App.P. 4(a)(1)). Filed with the clerk of the Supreme Court. Actual knowledge of entry shown by the appellant’s own affirmative action can start the clock without service (N.D.R.Civ.P. 58(b)(4)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Motion to extend appeal time
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Motion to extend appeal time: 30 days from Expiration of the 60-day period (N.D.R.App.P. 4(a)(4)). Excusable neglect or good cause; extension cannot exceed 30 days past the original deadline.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Cross-appeal or other party’s notice of appeal
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Cross-appeal or other party’s notice of appeal: 14 days from Filing of the first notice of appeal (or the regular time, if later) (N.D.R.App.P. 4(a)(2)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Notice of entry of judgment by prevailing party
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Notice of entry of judgment by prevailing party: 14 days from Entry of judgment (N.D.R.Civ.P. 58(b)(2)). Must include a copy of the judgment.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Renewed JMOL; motion to amend findings; motion to alter or amend
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Renewed JMOL; motion to amend findings; motion to alter or amend: 28 days from Notice of entry of judgment (N.D.R.Civ.P. 50(b), 52(b), 59(j)). Cannot be extended (N.D.R.Civ.P. 6(b)(2)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Motion for new trial (other than newly discovered evidence)
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Motion for new trial (other than newly discovered evidence): 60 days from Notice of entry of judgment (N.D.R.Civ.P. 59(c)(2)). The court may extend for good cause. Six months for newly discovered evidence. Rule 4(a)(3)(A) counts a new-trial motion filed within the time the civil rules allow, so a motion filed within this period appears to restart the appeal time; no case law on this point was researched.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Rule 60 motion that tolls appeal time
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Rule 60 motion that tolls appeal time: 28 days from Notice of entry of judgment (N.D.R.App.P. 4(a)(3)(A)(vi)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Attorney’s fees motion
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Attorney’s fees motion: 21 days from Notice of entry of judgment (N.D.R.Civ.P. 54(e)(2)(A)). A timely fee motion is a tolling motion under N.D.R.App.P. 4(a)(3)(A)(iii).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Transcript order
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Transcript order: 0 days from Filed with the notice of appeal (N.D.R.App.P. 10(b)(1)(E)). 21 days after the notice of appeal in cases assigned to post-judgment mediation (N.D.R.App.P. 5(d)(6)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Transcript advance payment
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Transcript advance payment: 14 days from Written cost estimate (N.D.R.App.P. 10(c)(3)). Preparation is suspended if not paid.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Transcript filed
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Transcript filed: 60 days from Transmission of the transcript order to district court staff (N.D.R.App.P. 10(c)(1), (d)(2)). District court may extend to no more than 90 days total.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 40 days from Filing of the transcript (or of the notice of appeal if no transcript) (N.D.R.App.P. 31(a)). 38-page limit.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 30 days from Service of the appellant’s brief (N.D.R.App.P. 31(a)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Reply brief: 14 days from Service of the appellee’s brief (N.D.R.App.P. 31(a)). Must be filed at least 5 days before argument if argument is less than 14 days away; 12-page limit.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Response to a motion
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Response to a motion: 14 days from Service of the motion (N.D.R.App.P. 27(b)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Notice of intent to participate in oral argument
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Notice of intent to participate in oral argument: 5 days from Service of the notice of oral argument (N.D.R.App.P. 34(a)(3)). Only for a party that did not request argument.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Petition for rehearing
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Petition for rehearing: 14 days from Entry of judgment (N.D.R.App.P. 40(a)(1)). 10-page limit.

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Mandate issues
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Mandate issues: 21 days from Entry of judgment (or 7 days after denial of rehearing) (N.D.R.App.P. 41(b)).

docs.t: North Dakota appeal deadline — Petition for Supreme Court review of a Court of Appeals decision
docs.x: North Dakota appellate deadline. Petition for Supreme Court review of a Court of Appeals decision: 14 days from Filing of the Court of Appeals judgment or order (or disposition of rehearing) (N.D. Sup. Ct. Admin. R. 27, § 13(a)). Supporting brief of no more than 10 pages filed with the petition.

docs.t: Nebraska — Serve every defendant within 180 days or the case dismisses itself
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Serve every defendant within 180 days or the case dismisses itself: An action is commenced when the complaint is filed. Each defendant must be properly served within 180 days, or the action against that defendant is dismissed without prejudice by operation of law the day after the time expires. The Revisor’s annotations describe the statute as self-executing; courts cannot extend it. (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-217 and annotations)

docs.t: Nebraska — A notice of appeal filed before a post-trial motion is decided is void
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. A notice of appeal filed before a post-trial motion is decided is void: A timely motion for new trial, to alter or amend, or to set aside the verdict (each due 10 days after entry of judgment) terminates the 30-day appeal time for all parties. A notice of appeal filed before the court announces its decision on such a motion has no effect, whether it was filed before or after the motion. You must file a new notice within 30 days after entry of the order ruling on the motion (no new fee). Unlike FRAP 4(a)(4)(B)(i), the early notice does not ripen. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-1912(3), 25-1144.01, 25-1329, 25-1315.02)

docs.t: Nebraska — Order the bill of exceptions with the notice of appeal, or lose it
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Order the bill of exceptions with the notice of appeal, or lose it: The appellant must file the request for the bill of exceptions (the transcript of the evidence) in the trial court at the same time as the notice of appeal. A late request is a waiver unless the appellate court grants leave for good cause outside the party’s reasonable control. Separately, file the transcript request designating each pleading by name and filing date; generalized “all documents” requests are not allowed. (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. §§ 2-105(B)(2)(a), (f), 2-104(A)(1))

docs.t: Nebraska — Errors not separately assigned are not reviewed
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Errors not separately assigned are not reviewed: The appellant’s brief must include a separate, concise statement of each claimed error, separately numbered and paragraphed. Review is limited to errors both assigned and discussed in the brief; plain error is reviewed only at the court’s option. Cross-appeals go in a separate section of the appellee’s brief titled “Brief on Cross-Appeal.” (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-109(D)(1)(e), (D)(4); Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1919)

docs.t: Nebraska — Excessive or inadequate damages need a new-trial motion
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Excessive or inadequate damages need a new-trial motion: In a jury case, a motion for new trial is not required to challenge the sufficiency of the evidence, but it is a prerequisite to appellate review of inadequate or excessive damages. The motion is due 10 days after entry of judgment. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-1912.01(2), 25-1144.01)

docs.t: Nebraska — Do not plead a dollar amount for general damages
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Do not plead a dollar amount for general damages: A complaint must not state the amount of general damages. It must state each category and the total of special damages, and if you want prejudgment interest, the date from which it runs. (Neb. Ct. R. Pldg. § 6-1108(a)(3)(A)-(C))

docs.t: Nebraska — Improper venue is a motion to transfer, not a Rule 12(b)(3) dismissal
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Improper venue is a motion to transfer, not a Rule 12(b)(3) dismissal: Section 6-1112(b)(3) is “pendency of another action,” not venue. A venue objection is raised by a timely motion to transfer to a proper county. The transferee court may order the plaintiff or its lawyer to pay the defendant’s expenses, including attorney’s fees. (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-403.01; Neb. Ct. R. Pldg. § 6-1112(b)(3) & cmt. [7])

docs.t: Nebraska — Answer in 30 days, and only one pre-answer motion
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Answer in 30 days, and only one pre-answer motion: The answer is due 30 days after service, not 21. A party that files a § 6-1112 motion cannot file a second pre-answer motion raising a defense that was available but omitted. That applies even to failure to state a claim on a new ground, which must instead be raised in the answer, by motion for judgment on the pleadings, or at trial. (Neb. Ct. R. Pldg. § 6-1112(a)(1)(A), (g)(2), (h)(2) & cmts. [11]-[12])

docs.t: Nebraska — Summary judgment: evidence is offered at a hearing, with indexes and annotated statements
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Summary judgment: evidence is offered at a hearing, with indexes and annotated statements: Serve the motion at least 10 days before the hearing; the opponent may serve affidavits before the hearing day. In district court, the movant must file and serve an Evidence Index and an Annotated Statement of Undisputed Facts with pinpoint cites. The opponent files an Evidence Index and an Annotated Statement of Disputed Facts. Leaving out the statement can be grounds to deny (or grant) the motion. Do not put these documents in the brief, and do not file discovery materials; offer them as evidence at the hearing. (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1332(1); Neb. Ct. R. § 6-1526; Neb. Ct. R. Pldg. § 6-1105 cmt. [9])

docs.t: Nebraska — Nonparty document subpoenas need 14 days’ notice to the parties first
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Nonparty document subpoenas need 14 days’ notice to the parties first: Before issuing a subpoena for documents or entry to a nonparty, serve every party with written notice at least 14 days before issuance. Any party may object, and then the subpoena may not command the objected-to items until the objection is withdrawn or overruled. Serve the subpoena at least 14 days before the production date, with copies to the other parties. The nonparty may object in writing within 14 days. (Neb. Ct. R. Disc. § 6-334(A)(b)-(e))

docs.t: Nebraska — Expert disclosures are due by default 180 days after the first answer
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Expert disclosures are due by default 180 days after the first answer: Since 2025, Nebraska requires federal-style expert disclosures, with signed reports from retained experts. Absent a court order or stipulation, they are due within 180 days after the first responsive pleading is served, and rebuttal disclosures within 45 days after the other side’s disclosure. A treating physician need not write a report merely because the testimony covers causation or prognosis. (Neb. Ct. R. Disc. § 6-326(c)(1)-(2))

docs.t: Nebraska — Supersedeas and cost bond within 30 days
docs.x: Nebraska land mine. Supersedeas and cost bond within 30 days: An appeal does not stay a money judgment unless, within 30 days after entry, the appellant posts a supersedeas bond, U.S. Government bonds, or cash. The amount is the lesser of the judgment plus costs and estimated interest, 50% of the appellant’s net worth, or $50 million. If there is no supersedeas bond, a $75 cost bond or cash deposit is due within 30 days. If it is not given, the appeal may be dismissed on motion. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-1916(1), 25-1914; Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-101(G)(2))

docs.t: Nebraska anti-SLAPP — Statute: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-21,241 to 25-21,246 (1994), narrow in scope
docs.x: Nebraska anti-SLAPP. Statute: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-21,241 to 25-21,246 (1994), narrow in scope: Nebraska’s anti-SLAPP law covers only an “action involving public petition and participation”: a claim, cross-claim, or counterclaim for damages brought by a “public applicant or permittee” (someone who applied for or obtained a permit, zoning change, lease, license, certificate, or other permission from a government body, or someone affiliated with that person) that is materially related to the defendant’s efforts to report on, comment on, rule on, challenge, or oppose the application or permission. It does not reach speech on public issues generally. The statute dates from Laws 1994, LB 665, and the chapter 25 index on the Legislature’s site shows no newer anti-SLAPP or Uniform Public Expression Protection Act sections. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-21,241(4), 25-21,242(1), (4))

docs.t: Nebraska anti-SLAPP — Procedure: an ordinary motion to dismiss or for summary judgment with a shifted burden; no deadline, no discovery stay
docs.x: Nebraska anti-SLAPP. Procedure: an ordinary motion to dismiss or for summary judgment with a shifted burden; no deadline, no discovery stay: A motion to dismiss for failure to state a cause of action must be granted once the movant shows the claim is an action involving public petition and participation, unless the responding party shows the claim has a substantial basis in law or is supported by a substantial argument to extend, modify, or reverse existing law. A summary-judgment motion works the same way, except the respondent must show a substantial basis in fact and law. The court must expedite the motion to dismiss and give both motions preference in hearing. The statute sets no filing deadline and does not stay discovery. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-21,245, 25-21,246)

docs.t: Nebraska anti-SLAPP — Heightened standard for the plaintiff’s damages
docs.x: Nebraska anti-SLAPP. Heightened standard for the plaintiff’s damages: In such an action, the plaintiff may recover damages only by proving by clear and convincing evidence that the communication was made knowing it was false or with reckless disregard of whether it was false, when truth or falsity is material to the claim. (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-21,244(1))

docs.t: Nebraska anti-SLAPP — Fees and damages require a separate claim, not a motion
docs.x: Nebraska anti-SLAPP. Fees and damages require a separate claim, not a motion: There is no automatic fee award on a successful motion. The defendant must bring its own action, claim, cross-claim, or counterclaim. Costs and attorney’s fees are recoverable on showing the suit was commenced or continued without a substantial basis in fact and law and could not be supported by a substantial argument for changing the law. Other compensatory damages also require proof that the suit was brought to harass, intimidate, punish, or maliciously inhibit petition, speech, or association. The right may be waived only by a specific waiver. The Revisor’s annotation notes that the trial court decides the first showing as a matter of law (Sand Livestock Sys. v. Svoboda, 17 Neb. App. 28 (2008)). (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-21,243 and annotation)

docs.t: Nebraska anti-SLAPP — Appeal: no special right
docs.x: Nebraska anti-SLAPP. Appeal: no special right: The statute gives no immediate appeal from denial of an anti-SLAPP motion. Denial of a motion to dismiss or for summary judgment is not among the listed final orders (the only listed summary-judgment denial is one based on sovereign or official immunity), so review would normally wait for final judgment. No case law on this point was researched. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-21,245, 25-21,246, 25-1902(1))

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Notice of appeal and docket fee (district court civil judgment)
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Notice of appeal and docket fee (district court civil judgment): 30 days from Entry of the judgment, decree, or final order (clerk’s file stamp date) (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-1912(1), 25-1301(3)). Filed in the district court. The notice and fee are the only jurisdictional steps. No extension provision appears in § 25-1912.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Request for bill of exceptions; transcript request
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Request for bill of exceptions; transcript request: 0 days from Same time as the notice of appeal (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. §§ 2-105(B)(2)(a), 2-104(A)(1)). A late bill-of-exceptions request is a waiver absent appellate leave for good cause outside the party’s control.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Appellee’s supplemental (or substitute) bill of exceptions request
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Appellee’s supplemental (or substitute) bill of exceptions request: 10 days from Service of the appellant’s request (or the notice of appeal, if the appellant requested none) (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-105(B)(2)(e)-(f)).

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Motion for new trial / to alter or amend / to set aside verdict
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Motion for new trial / to alter or amend / to set aside verdict: 10 days from Entry of judgment (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-1144.01, 25-1329, 25-1315.02). A timely motion terminates the appeal time for all parties. An earlier notice of appeal is void; refile within 30 days after entry of the ruling.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Notice of appeal after a tolling motion
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Notice of appeal after a tolling motion: 30 days from Entry of the order ruling on the motion (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1912(3)). No additional fee.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Cost bond or $75 cash deposit
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Cost bond or $75 cash deposit: 30 days from Entry of judgment or of the order overruling a new-trial motion (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1914). Not needed if a supersedeas bond is given. The appeal may be dismissed on motion if missing.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Supersedeas bond to stay execution
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Supersedeas bond to stay execution: 30 days from Entry of the judgment, decree, or final order (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1916). Lesser of judgment-based amount, 50% of net worth, or $50 million for money judgments.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Appeal from denial of summary judgment based on sovereign or official immunity
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Appeal from denial of summary judgment based on sovereign or official immunity: 30 days from Entry of the order (or entry of judgment) (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1902(1)(d), (2)).

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 30 days from Filing of the transcript in the appellate court (no bill requested) or the bill of exceptions due date (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-109(A)(1)). First extension up to 30 days on a general showing; later ones need good or exceptional cause.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief (including any cross-appeal)
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief (including any cross-appeal): 30 days from Appellant’s service and filing of its brief (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. §§ 2-109(A)(2), 2-101(E)). Add 3 days if served by mail.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Reply brief: 10 days from Appellee’s service and filing of its brief (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-109(A)(3)). Add 3 days if served by mail.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Response to a motion
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Response to a motion: 10 days from Filing of the motion (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-106(B)(2)). No reply allowed.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Motion for appellate attorney fees
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Motion for appellate attorney fees: 10 days from Release of the opinion or order disposing of the appeal (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-106(G)(2)). Unless a statute provides otherwise.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Motion for rehearing and supporting brief
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Motion for rehearing and supporting brief: 10 days from Release of the opinion or order disposing of the appeal (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-113(A)). Tolls the time to petition for further review from the Court of Appeals.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Petition for further review and memorandum brief
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Petition for further review and memorandum brief: 30 days from Release of the Court of Appeals opinion or entry of its final order, whichever is later (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-102(F)(1); Neb. Rev. Stat. § 24-1107). $50 docket fee; 3,500 words; responses due within 10 days.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Supplemental brief after further review is granted
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Supplemental brief after further review is granted: 20 days from Entry of the order granting further review (nonpetitioners: 20 days after the petitioner’s brief) (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-102(H)).

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Application to stay mandate pending U.S. Supreme Court review
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Application to stay mandate pending U.S. Supreme Court review: 7 days from Filing of the opinion or other dispositive entry (Neb. Ct. R. App. P. § 2-114(A)(2)). Must show that a federal question is involved.

docs.t: Nebraska appeal deadline — Appeal from county court to district court
docs.x: Nebraska appellate deadline. Appeal from county court to district court: 30 days from Entry of the county court judgment or final order (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-2729(1)). Notice and district court docket fee are filed with the county court clerk. The statement of errors is due 20 days after the bill of exceptions is filed (30 days after the notice if no bill) (§ 6-1518(B)).

docs.t: New Mexico — Excuse the judge in 10 days, and before asking the judge for anything
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Excuse the judge in 10 days, and before asking the judge for anything: The peremptory-excusal clock is 10 days: from notice of assignment for plaintiffs, and from the first Rule 1-012 filing for defendants. The 120-day outer cap and the bar after any hearing or request to the judge apply on top of that. Co-defendants sharing a firm get only one excusal between them. (Rule 1-088.1 NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Counting days: 10 or fewer skips weekends; 11 or more counts every day
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Counting days: 10 or fewer skips weekends; 11 or more counts every day: Periods of 10 days or less exclude intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. Periods of 11 days or more count every day. Three days are added for mail service, but not to appeal, rehearing, or certiorari deadlines. (Rules 1-006, 12-308, 12-201(A)(2), 12-404(A), 12-502(B) NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Notice of appeal: 30 days from filing in the clerk’s office, with no mail days
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Notice of appeal: 30 days from filing in the clerk’s office, with no mail days: The 30 days run from when the judgment is filed in the district court clerk’s office. Only a timely motion that could affect finality restarts the clock (Rule 1-060(B) motions only if filed within 30 days of judgment). An order granting a new trial is not appealable and makes the earlier judgment non-appealable. Extensions must be sought within 30 days after the deadline, can add at most 30 days, and a notice of appeal must still be filed within those 30 days even if the motion is pending. (Rule 12-201(A), (D), (E) NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Trial counsel owes the docketing statement in 30 days
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Trial counsel owes the docketing statement in 30 days: In the Court of Appeals, trial counsel must file the docketing statement within 30 days after the notice of appeal, with the docket fee. Conclusory issue statements are rejected. Issues and preservation must be stated specifically, because on the summary calendar the court decides on the docketing statement and record alone. (Rules 12-208(A), (B), (D), (H), 12-210(D) NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Answer a proposed summary disposition within 20 days
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Answer a proposed summary disposition within 20 days: If the case is placed on the summary calendar, the parties have 20 days from service of the notice of proposed summary disposition to file a memorandum in opposition or support. The limit is 35 pages or 11,000 words, and no new issues may be raised outside the docketing statement unless the court allows an amendment. There is no oral argument. (Rule 12-210(D) NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Anti-SLAPP fees depend on filing within 90 days of the answer
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Anti-SLAPP fees depend on filing within 90 days of the answer: Mandatory fees follow only if the protection is pleaded as an affirmative defense and the dispositive motion is filed within ninety days after the movant’s answer. The statute reaches only speech at public hearings or meetings in quasi-judicial proceedings before state or local bodies, and it does not apply in federal diversity cases. (NMSA 1978, § 38-2-9.1(A), (B), (D))

docs.t: New Mexico — Pro hac vice: 5 registrations a year, and local counsel must physically attend
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Pro hac vice: 5 registrations a year, and local counsel must physically attend: Register with the State Bar (not the court) for each matter: $500 for the first registration and $375 for each later one in a calendar year, with a maximum of five a year. Then file the Rule 1-089.1 affidavit with your first paper. New Mexico counsel must be present in person at all proceedings unless excused. (Rules 24-106(A), (D), 1-089.1 NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Uninsured lawyers, including pro hac vice lawyers, must give written notice
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Uninsured lawyers, including pro hac vice lawyers, must give written notice: If your malpractice coverage is below $100,000 per claim and $300,000 aggregate, you must give the client the prescribed notice and get a signed acknowledgment. This applies to lawyers practicing under Rule 24-106. (Rule 16-104(C)(1), (3) NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Summary-judgment papers: numbered facts, 15-day response
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Summary-judgment papers: numbered facts, 15-day response: The movant lists numbered material facts with record citations. The opponent responds within 15 days with numbered disputed facts keyed to the movant’s numbers, and any fact not specifically controverted is deemed admitted. The reply is due within 15 days. Opposed motions generally must recite that concurrence was sought. (Rules 1-056, 1-007.1 NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Shorter post-trial and responsive-pleading clocks than federal practice
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Shorter post-trial and responsive-pleading clocks than federal practice: Motions for new trial or to alter or amend judgment are due within 30 days after entry of judgment. After a Rule 1-012 motion is denied, the answer is due in 10 days. A jury demand is due within 10 days after the last pleading directed to the issue, with a $150 or $300 jury fee, or the jury is waived. (Rules 1-059, 1-012(A), 1-038 NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Two years of inactivity can mean dismissal with prejudice
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Two years of inactivity can mean dismissal with prejudice: Any party may move to dismiss a claim with prejudice if no significant action toward trial or final disposition has been taken within 2 years after filing. Without a scheduling order, the court may also dismiss without prejudice after 180 days of inactivity, with 30 days to seek reinstatement. (Rule 1-041(E) NMRA)

docs.t: New Mexico — Appellate amendments take effect December 31, 2026
docs.x: New Mexico land mine. Appellate amendments take effect December 31, 2026: Orders approved October 30, 2026 amend Rules 12-202, 12-208, 12-209, 12-211, 12-503, 12-505, 12-601 to 12-603 and add Rules 12-208.1, 12-211.1, and 12-502.1, for cases filed on or after December 31, 2026. Examples: in criminal, delinquency, and Children’s Code cases the notice of appeal is no longer served on the appellate court (other cases still serve it); the district court clerk must file the record proper within 5 days (was 14) after receiving the docketing statement; and the appellant pays record costs within 5 days after the clerk files the statement of costs. Check which version governs your case. (Order No. S-1-RCR-2023-00005; Rules 12-202(E), 12-209(C) NMRA as amended (eff. Dec. 31, 2026))

docs.t: New Mexico anti-SLAPP — Narrow anti-SLAPP statute: only speech at public hearings or meetings in quasi-judicial proceedings
docs.x: New Mexico anti-SLAPP. Narrow anti-SLAPP statute: only speech at public hearings or meetings in quasi-judicial proceedings: NMSA 1978, § 38-2-9.1 (Laws 2001, ch. 218) covers only actions for money damages based on conduct or speech “in connection with a public hearing or public meeting in a quasi-judicial proceeding” before a tribunal or decision-making body of a political subdivision. A “public meeting in a quasi-judicial proceeding” includes meetings or presentations before state, city, town, or village councils, planning commissions, and review boards or commissions (§ 38-2-9.1(D)). This is not a general public-participation statute like California’s. Section 38-2-9.2 states the legislative findings. (NMSA 1978, §§ 38-2-9.1(A), (D), 38-2-9.2)

docs.t: New Mexico anti-SLAPP — Procedure: a special motion, Rule 12 motion, or summary judgment, heard on a priority basis
docs.x: New Mexico anti-SLAPP. Procedure: a special motion, Rule 12 motion, or summary judgment, heard on a priority basis: A covered action is subject to a special motion to dismiss, a motion for judgment on the pleadings, or a motion for summary judgment, which the court must consider “on a priority or expedited basis.” The statute sets no discovery stay, no burden-shifting test, and no deadline for a hearing. The annotations report that courts apply it only where the speech or conduct was in connection with a qualifying proceeding. Examples: a district-court hearing on a recall petition is judicial, not quasi-judicial (Cordova v. Cline, 2013-NMCA-083). Campaign mailers are not covered (Chandler v. Advance N.M. Now PAC, 2021-NMCA-017). Statements to a federal agency are not covered (Ferebee v. Hume, 2021-NMCA-012). (NMSA 1978, § 38-2-9.1(A); annotations to § 38-2-9.1 (2026 NMSA))

docs.t: New Mexico anti-SLAPP — Fees: mandatory if the motion is filed within 90 days of the answer and granted
docs.x: New Mexico anti-SLAPP. Fees: mandatory if the motion is filed within 90 days of the answer and granted: If the defendant raises the statute’s protection as an affirmative defense, and the court grants a motion to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, or for summary judgment that was filed within ninety days after the moving party’s answer, the court shall award reasonable attorney fees and costs. If the court finds the special motion or summary-judgment motion frivolous or solely intended to cause delay, it shall award fees and costs to the party prevailing on the motion. The annotations report that fees are a sanction, cover appellate work, and carry no prejudgment interest (Cordova v. Cline, 2021-NMCA-022). (NMSA 1978, § 38-2-9.1(B); annotations (Cordova v. Cline, 2021-NMCA-022))

docs.t: New Mexico anti-SLAPP — Expedited appeal for any party
docs.x: New Mexico anti-SLAPP. Expedited appeal for any party: Any party has a right to an expedited appeal from an order on the special motions, or from the trial court’s failure to rule on an expedited basis. The annotations report that the appeal covers rulings on whether the statute applies (Ferebee v. Hume, 2021-NMCA-012) and is limited to speech-based defenses (Valenzuela v. My Way Holdings, LLC, 2024-NMCA-009). The statute sets no separate appeal deadline, so the general rules apply. (NMSA 1978, § 38-2-9.1(C); annotations)

docs.t: New Mexico anti-SLAPP — Not available in federal court; no UPEPA found
docs.x: New Mexico anti-SLAPP. Not available in federal court; no UPEPA found: Per the annotation, the Tenth Circuit held § 38-2-9.1 procedural and inapplicable in federal diversity cases (Los Lobos Renewable Power, LLC v. Americulture, Inc., 885 F.3d 659 (10th Cir. 2018)). The current NMSA Chapter 38 (compiled November 2026) contains no Uniform Public Expression Protection Act, and the 2026 table of newly enacted sections lists none. 2025 session laws were not separately checked, but a 2025 enactment would normally appear in the current Chapter 38. (Annotation to NMSA 1978, § 38-2-9.2; NMSA Ch. 38 (2026); Laws 2026 new-sections table)

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (civil)
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (civil): 30 days from Filing of the judgment or order in the district court clerk’s office (Rule 12-201(A)(1)(b) NMRA). No 3-day mail extension. Filed in district court.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Notice of appeal by another party (cross-appeal)
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Notice of appeal by another party (cross-appeal): 14 days from Service of the first notice of appeal (or the original 30 days, if later) (Rule 12-201(B)(1) NMRA).

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Motion to extend time to appeal
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Motion to extend time to appeal: 30 days from Expiration of the original appeal deadline (Rule 12-201(E) NMRA). Excusable neglect after the deadline. The extension cannot exceed 30 days past the original deadline.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Motion for new trial / to alter or amend judgment
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Motion for new trial / to alter or amend judgment: 30 days from Entry of judgment (Rule 1-059 NMRA). Tolls the time to appeal (Rule 12-201(D)).

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Docketing statement (Court of Appeals)
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Docketing statement (Court of Appeals): 30 days from Filing of the notice of appeal (or the date a premature notice becomes effective) (Rule 12-208(B) NMRA). Filed by trial counsel, with the docket fee.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Memorandum opposing a proposed summary disposition
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Memorandum opposing a proposed summary disposition: 20 days from Service of the notice of proposed summary disposition (Rule 12-210(D)(2) NMRA). 35 pages or 11,000 words.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Brief in chief (general calendar)
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Brief in chief (general calendar): 45 days from Service of notice that transcripts are filed, or the notice of non-designation (Rule 12-210(C)(2)(a) NMRA).

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Answer brief (general calendar)
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Answer brief (general calendar): 45 days from Service of the brief in chief (Rule 12-210(C)(2)(b) NMRA).

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Reply brief: 20 days from Service of the answer brief (Rule 12-210(C)(2)(c), (E)(2)(c) NMRA). Optional.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Brief in chief (legal calendar)
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Brief in chief (legal calendar): 30 days from Service of the calendar assignment notice (Rule 12-210(E)(2)(a) NMRA). Answer brief due 30 days after the brief in chief.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Application for interlocutory appeal
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Application for interlocutory appeal: 15 days from Entry of the certified interlocutory order (Rule 12-203(A) NMRA). Filed in the appellate court. No mail days.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Motion for rehearing
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Motion for rehearing: 15 days from Filing of the appellate disposition (Rule 12-404(A) NMRA). No mail days.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Petition for writ of certiorari to the Supreme Court
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Petition for writ of certiorari to the Supreme Court: 30 days from Final action by the Court of Appeals (decision, or ruling on a timely rehearing motion) (Rule 12-502(B) NMRA). 10 pages or 3,150 words. No mail days.

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Response to certiorari petition / conditional cross-petition
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Response to certiorari petition / conditional cross-petition: 15 days from Service of the petition (response: or the grant) (Rule 12-502(G), (H) NMRA).

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Certiorari to Court of Appeals in administrative cases
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Certiorari to Court of Appeals in administrative cases: 30 days from District court’s final action (Rule 12-505(C) NMRA).

docs.t: New Mexico appeal deadline — Appeal from magistrate or metropolitan court to district court
docs.x: New Mexico appellate deadline. Appeal from magistrate or metropolitan court to district court: 15 days from Filing of the lower-court judgment (Rule 1-072 NMRA). Trial de novo cases.

docs.t: Ohio — Filing is not commencement unless service is obtained within one year
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Filing is not commencement unless service is obtained within one year: An Ohio action is ‘commenced’ by filing only if service is obtained on a named defendant within one year of filing. Late service can mean the limitations period was never stopped. (Civ.R. 3(A))

docs.t: Ohio — Do not state a dollar amount above $25,000
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Do not state a dollar amount above $25,000: A pleading seeking more than $25,000 must say so but may not state the amount. (Civ.R. 8(A))

docs.t: Ohio — Medical-claim complaints need an affidavit of merit
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Medical-claim complaints need an affidavit of merit: A complaint with a medical, dental, optometric, or chiropractic claim must include an affidavit of merit from a qualified expert for each defendant who needs expert proof. Any motion to extend must be filed with the complaint, and extensions are capped at 90 days except as the rule allows. (Civ.R. 10(D)(2))

docs.t: Ohio — Continuance motions must be signed by the client too
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Continuance motions must be signed by the client too: A motion to continue a trial or hearing must be written, state the reason, and be endorsed by the party as well as counsel, unless the judge waives this for good cause. (Civ.R. 6(B)(2)(b))

docs.t: Ohio — Object to the magistrate within 14 days or lose the issue
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Object to the magistrate within 14 days or lose the issue: Failing to file specific objections to a magistrate’s decision within 14 days forfeits appellate review of the adopted findings and conclusions, except for plain error. (Civ.R. 53(D)(3)(b)(i), (iv))

docs.t: Ohio — 30 days to appeal, with no extension
docs.x: Ohio land mine. 30 days to appeal, with no extension: The notice of appeal is due in the trial court within 30 days of entry of judgment, and the court of appeals cannot extend it. The clock starts later only if the clerk failed to serve notice of the judgment within 3 days, or after listed post-judgment motions (Civ.R. 50(B), 59, magistrate objections, findings requests, attorney-fee and prejudgment-interest motions) are resolved. Civ.R. 60(B) motions are not on the tolling list. (App.R. 4(A), (B)(2); App.R. 14(B))

docs.t: Ohio — Assignments of error must be stated and argued separately
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Assignments of error must be stated and argued separately: The court of appeals may disregard an assignment of error that does not identify the error in the record or is not argued separately in the brief. (App.R. 12(A)(2); App.R. 16(A)(3), (7))

docs.t: Ohio — Supreme Court deadlines are hard: 45 days, no extensions, memorandum filed with the notice
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Supreme Court deadlines are hard: 45 days, no extensions, memorandum filed with the notice: A discretionary appeal requires both a notice of appeal and a 15-page memorandum in support of jurisdiction within 45 days of the court of appeals’ entry. The Clerk refuses late filings, and the Court will not extend this time. A motion to certify a conflict in the court of appeals does not extend the 45 days. (S.Ct.Prac.R. 3.02(B), 3.03(B)(1), 7.01(A)(1), 7.02(B); App.R. 25(A))

docs.t: Ohio — Pro hac vice is capped and has hidden renewal deadlines
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Pro hac vice is capped and has hidden renewal deadlines: Three new proceedings per calendar year, $500 registration before moving, a 30-day post-grant notice, and a $500 renewal each January for pending cases. Missing a notice or renewal means automatic exclusion. (Gov.Bar R. XII, Sections 2(A)(3), 2(A)(5), 4, 5)

docs.t: Ohio — Judge disqualification goes to Columbus, at least 7 days out
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Judge disqualification goes to Columbus, at least 7 days out: The affidavit of disqualification is filed with the Clerk of the Supreme Court, not the trial court, at least 7 calendar days before the next hearing. It must be notarized and served, or the Clerk rejects it. (R.C. 2701.03(B), (C)(2))

docs.t: Ohio — Two notice dismissals operate as an adjudication on the merits
docs.x: Ohio land mine. Two notice dismissals operate as an adjudication on the merits: A plaintiff’s Civ.R. 41(A)(1) notice dismissal is without prejudice, but a notice dismissal of a claim the plaintiff has already dismissed once in any court is an adjudication on the merits. (Civ.R. 41(A)(1))

docs.t: Ohio — UPEPA motion due 60 days after service
docs.x: Ohio land mine. UPEPA motion due 60 days after service: The anti-SLAPP motion for expedited relief must be filed within 60 days after service of the pleading (extendable for good cause). Filing stays discovery, and a granted motion carries mandatory fees. (R.C. 2747.02, 2747.03, 2747.05(A))

docs.t: Ohio anti-SLAPP — Statute: Ohio’s Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (effective April 9, 2025)
docs.x: Ohio anti-SLAPP. Statute: Ohio’s Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (effective April 9, 2025): Ohio adopted the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (UPEPA) as R.C. Chapter 2747 (S.B. 237, 135th General Assembly), effective April 9, 2025. It applies to civil actions filed, and claims asserted, on or after that date. It covers claims based on a person’s (1) communication in a legislative, executive, judicial, administrative, or other governmental proceeding; (2) communication on an issue under consideration in such a proceeding; or (3) exercise of speech, press, assembly, petition, or association rights under the U.S. or Ohio Constitution on a matter of public concern. The General Assembly says it intends substantive immunity from suit, not just immunity from liability. Courts must construe the Act broadly and consider uniformity with other UPEPA states. (R.C. 2747.01(B), (E); R

docs.t: Ohio anti-SLAPP — What the Act does not cover
docs.x: Ohio anti-SLAPP. What the Act does not cover: Exempt: (1) claims against a governmental unit or its employee or agent acting in an official capacity; (2) government enforcement actions to protect against an imminent threat to public health or safety; (3) claims against a person primarily engaged in selling or leasing goods or services when the claim arises from communications about that sale or lease (creative, journalistic, political, and artistic works are not ‘goods or services’); (4) survivorship, bodily-injury, and wrongful-death claims, and statements about them. The responding party bears the burden of proving an exemption applies. (R.C. 2747.01(A)(1), (C); R.C. 2747.04(C)(2))

docs.t: Ohio anti-SLAPP — Procedure: 60-day motion, automatic stay, 60-day hearing, 60-day ruling
docs.x: Ohio anti-SLAPP. Procedure: 60-day motion, automatic stay, 60-day hearing, 60-day ruling: File a ‘motion for expedited relief’ within 60 days after service of the complaint, counterclaim, cross-claim, third-party claim, or other pleading asserting the claim; the court may extend this for good cause. Filing stays all other proceedings between the movant and the responding party, including discovery and pending motions. The stay lasts until 30 days after the ruling or the end of any appeal, whichever is later; during an appeal, everything in the action is stayed for all parties. The court may allow limited, specific discovery needed to meet a burden, may hear unrelated motions or public-safety injunction requests for good cause, and fee motions are not stayed. The hearing must be held within 60 days after filing (later if discovery is allowed or for good cause), and the court must rule wit

docs.t: Ohio anti-SLAPP — Standard: three steps; Rule 56-type evidence
docs.x: Ohio anti-SLAPP. Standard: three steps; Rule 56-type evidence: The court considers the pleadings, motion, response, and any evidence usable on summary judgment under Civ.R. 56. It must dismiss with prejudice if (1) the movant shows the claim is based on protected activity; (2) the respondent fails to show an exemption; and (3) either the respondent fails to establish a prima facie case on each essential element, or the movant shows failure to state a claim or no genuine issue of material fact and entitlement to judgment as a matter of law. A voluntary dismissal without prejudice does not defeat the movant’s right to a ruling for fee purposes; a dismissal with prejudice makes the movant the prevailing party. (R.C. 2747.04(B), (C), (E))

docs.t: Ohio anti-SLAPP — Fees: mandatory for a winning movant; only for frivolous motions against one
docs.x: Ohio anti-SLAPP. Fees: mandatory for a winning movant; only for frivolous motions against one: If the motion is granted, the court must award the movant reasonable attorney’s fees, court costs, and other reasonable litigation expenses, and may not reduce them because the representation was pro bono or contingent. If the motion is denied and the court finds it was frivolous conduct under R.C. 2323.51, the respondent gets its fees and expenses, but only after any appeal affirming the denial. (R.C. 2747.05(A)-(B))

docs.t: Ohio anti-SLAPP — Appeal: denial is a final order; 30 days
docs.x: Ohio anti-SLAPP. Appeal: denial is a final order; 30 days: A denial is a final, appealable order, giving the movant an interlocutory appeal. The appeal must be filed within 30 days after entry of the order. R.C. 2505.02(B)(9) separately lists an order denying a motion for expedited relief under R.C. 2747.04 as a final order. The statute gives no corresponding immediate appeal from a grant; a grant that disposes of fewer than all claims is subject to the usual final-order and Civ.R. 54(B) rules. (R.C. 2747.05(C); R.C. 2505.02(B)(9); Civ.R. 54(B))

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Notice of appeal to court of appeals (civil)
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Notice of appeal to court of appeals (civil): 30 days from Entry of the final judgment or order (or clerk’s actual service if not made within Civ.R. 58(B)’s 3 days) (App.R. 4(A)). Filed in the trial court. The court of appeals cannot extend it (App.R. 14(B)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Notice of appeal by another party / cross-appeal
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Notice of appeal by another party / cross-appeal: 10 days from Filing of the first timely notice of appeal (or the original 30 days, if later) (App.R. 4(B)(1); App.R. 3(C)). Needed only if the appellee seeks to change the judgment.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Restarted appeal period after tolling motions
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Restarted appeal period after tolling motions: 30 days from Entry of the order resolving the last timely Civ.R. 50(B), 59, magistrate-objection, findings, attorney-fee, or prejudgment-interest filing (App.R. 4(B)(2)). Civ.R. 60(B) motions do not toll.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Civ.R. 50(B) JNOV / Civ.R. 59 new-trial motion
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Civ.R. 50(B) JNOV / Civ.R. 59 new-trial motion: 28 days from Entry of judgment (or the clerk’s actual service if late) (Civ.R. 50(B); Civ.R. 59(B)). Cannot be extended (Civ.R. 6(B)(2)(e)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Objections to magistrate’s decision
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Objections to magistrate’s decision: 14 days from Filing of the magistrate’s decision (Civ.R. 53(D)(3)(b)(i)). Failure to object forfeits all but plain-error review.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — App.R. 9(B)(5) transcript statement / docketing statement
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. App.R. 9(B)(5) transcript statement / docketing statement: 0 days from Filed with the notice of appeal (App.R. 9(B)(5); App.R. 3(H)). The record is deemed complete if not filed within 10 days of the notice (App.R. 10(B)(7)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Appellee’s designation of additional transcript
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Appellee’s designation of additional transcript: 10 days from Service of the appellant’s App.R. 9(B)(5) statement (App.R. 9(B)(5)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Transmission of record
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Transmission of record: 40 days from Filing of the last notice of appeal (App.R. 10(A)). 20 days on the accelerated calendar. Extensions must be requested before the period expires.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 20 days from Clerk’s mailing of notice that the record was filed (App.R. 18(A)). 15 days on the accelerated calendar (App.R. 11.1(C)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 20 days from Service of the appellant’s brief (App.R. 18(A)). 15 days on the accelerated calendar.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Reply brief: 10 days from Service of the appellee’s brief (App.R. 18(A)). Not allowed on the accelerated calendar unless ordered.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Response to motion in court of appeals
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Response to motion in court of appeals: 10 days from Service of the motion (App.R. 15(A)). Reply in 7 days.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Application for reconsideration / en banc
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Application for reconsideration / en banc: 15 days from Filing of the court of appeals’ judgment (App.R. 26(A)(1)(a), (A)(2)(c)). 15-page limit; response in 15 days.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Motion to certify a conflict
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Motion to certify a conflict: 10 days from Clerk’s mailing of the judgment and docket notation (App.R. 25(A)). Does not extend the 45-day Supreme Court deadline and cannot itself be extended.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Notice of appeal + memorandum in support of jurisdiction to Supreme Court
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Notice of appeal + memorandum in support of jurisdiction to Supreme Court: 45 days from Filing of the court of appeals’ judgment entry (S.Ct.Prac.R. 7.01(A)(1)). Mandatory; runs from the ruling on a timely App.R. 26(A) application. 15-page memorandum.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Memorandum in response to jurisdiction
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Memorandum in response to jurisdiction: 30 days from Filing of the memorandum in support (S.Ct.Prac.R. 7.03(A)). 20 days in parental-rights, adoption, and bail cases.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Certified-conflict filing in Supreme Court
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Certified-conflict filing in Supreme Court: 45 days from Date of the court of appeals’ order certifying the conflict (S.Ct.Prac.R. 8.01(D)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Supreme Court merit brief (appellant)
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Supreme Court merit brief (appellant): 40 days from Clerk’s filing of the record (S.Ct.Prac.R. 16.02(A)). Appellee 30 days later; reply 20 days later. 50/50/20-page limits.

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Supreme Court motion for reconsideration
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Supreme Court motion for reconsideration: 10 days from Filing of the judgment entry or order (S.Ct.Prac.R. 18.02(A)(1)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — Pro hac vice motion in Supreme Court
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. Pro hac vice motion in Supreme Court: 30 days from Filing of the appeal (or at least 30 days before oral argument) (S.Ct.Prac.R. 2.02(B)(3)-(4)).

docs.t: Ohio appeal deadline — UPEPA (anti-SLAPP) denial appeal
docs.x: Ohio appellate deadline. UPEPA (anti-SLAPP) denial appeal: 30 days from Entry of the order denying the motion for expedited relief (R.C. 2747.05(C)). Interlocutory appeal of right; all proceedings stayed during the appeal.

docs.t: Oklahoma — 180-day service deadline with automatic dismissal
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. 180-day service deadline with automatic dismissal: If a defendant is not served within 180 days after the petition is filed and good cause is not shown, the action is deemed dismissed without prejudice as to that defendant, and the court must enter a dismissal order within 200 days if no defendant was served. Refiling depends on the savings statute, 12 O.S. § 100. Relation back of a new defendant also turns on notice within the 180 days. (12 O.S. §§ 2004(I), 2015(C)(3))

docs.t: Oklahoma — Don’t plead a dollar figure above the diversity amount
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Don’t plead a dollar figure above the diversity amount: In non-contract cases seeking more than the 28 U.S.C. § 1332 amount, the petition must say only that damages exceed that amount; below it, state the exact amount. Punitive-damage petitions may not state a figure. Defendants can file a Motion to Clarify Damages before the pretrial order to test a below-threshold pleading for removal purposes. (12 O.S. §§ 2008(A), 2009(G)-(H))

docs.t: Oklahoma — A “reservation of time” waives your Rule 12-type defenses
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. A “reservation of time” waives your Rule 12-type defenses: The answer is due 20 days after service.
