Filing a reservation of time buys 20 more days but waives personal jurisdiction, venue, process, service, failure to state a claim, and capacity-to-be-sued defenses. A motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim that does not separately list each defect is denied without a hearing. (12 O.S. § 2012(A)(1), (B))

docs.t: Oklahoma — There is no notice of appeal
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. There is no notice of appeal: An appeal is commenced only by a petition in error filed with the Clerk of the Supreme Court within 30 days after the written, signed judgment is filed. Filing something in the trial court does not commence an appeal, and a minute entry, verdict, or letter ruling never starts or satisfies the clock. (12 O.S. §§ 990A(A), 696.2(D))

docs.t: Oklahoma — Post-trial motions toll only if filed within 10 days
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Post-trial motions toll only if filed within 10 days: A motion for new trial, JNOV, or to vacate or reconsider suspends the appeal time only if filed within 10 days after the judgment is filed; a motion to vacate filed on day 11 through 30 is allowed but does not extend the 30-day appeal clock. Fee and cost motions never do. (12 O.S. §§ 990.2(A)-(B), (D), 1031.1(B))

docs.t: Oklahoma — Interlocutory appeals by right need the record within 30 days too
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Interlocutory appeals by right need the record within 30 days too: For orders on injunctions, receivers, class certification, attachment, or granting a new trial, the petition in error and the record must both be filed with the Supreme Court within 30 days after the order is filed. (12 O.S. § 993(A))

docs.t: Oklahoma — Discovery response clocks wait for the answer
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Discovery response clocks wait for the answer: Interrogatories, document requests, and requests for admission may be served any time after the petition is filed, but the 30-day response period does not start until an answer to the petition is filed, unless the court orders otherwise or the parties agree in writing. (12 O.S. §§ 3233(A), 3234(B)(2)(a), 3236(A))

docs.t: Oklahoma — 30-question caps and a 6-hour, business-hours deposition
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. 30-question caps and a 6-hour, business-hours deposition: Interrogatories and requests for admission are each capped at 30 per party (subparts count separately for interrogatories). Depositions are limited to 6 hours between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on non-holiday weekdays unless agreed or ordered, and a nonparty need only attend in the county of residence, an adjoining county, or where served. (12 O.S. §§ 3230(A)(3), (B), 3233(A), 3236(A))

docs.t: Oklahoma — Expert depositions are usable at trial for any purpose
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Expert depositions are usable at trial for any purpose: Any expert witness’s deposition may be used at trial for any purpose without showing the expert is unavailable, and a witness who simply lives outside the county qualifies as unavailable — far looser than FRCP 32(a)(4). (12 O.S. § 3232(A)(3)(b), (e))

docs.t: Oklahoma — Rule 11 motions here can bring mandatory fees
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Rule 11 motions here can bring mandatory fees: Monetary sanctions, including the movant’s attorney fees, are mandatory for a paper presented for an improper purpose, and in non-contract cases the court must order fees against a party whose claim or defense it finds frivolous or knowingly false at the dismissal, summary-judgment, or merits stage. (12 O.S. §§ 2011(C)(2)(c), 2011.1)

docs.t: Oklahoma — Anti-SLAPP motion: 60 days from service, and it freezes discovery
docs.x: Oklahoma land mine. Anti-SLAPP motion: 60 days from service, and it freezes discovery: Defendants sued over speech, petitioning, or association must move under the Citizens Participation Act within 60 days after service; filing suspends discovery, and a win carries mandatory fees and sanctions. Plaintiffs need clear and specific evidence of every element. (12 O.S. §§ 1432, 1434, 1438)

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Statute: Oklahoma Citizens Participation Act
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Statute: Oklahoma Citizens Participation Act: 12 O.S. §§ 1430-1440, effective November 1, 2014, with exemptions amended in 2022 and 2025. It protects the rights to free speech (communication on a matter of public concern: health or safety, environmental, economic or community well-being, government, public officials or figures, or marketplace goods and services), to petition (broadly defined to include communications in or about judicial, official, legislative, and agency proceedings and efforts to get government to consider an issue), and of association. It is construed liberally and does not displace other defenses or immunities. (12 O.S. §§ 1430, 1431, 1440)

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Motion to dismiss: 60 days; discovery stops
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Motion to dismiss: 60 days; discovery stops: A party may move to dismiss a legal action (including a counterclaim or cross-claim) that is based on, relates to, or responds to its protected activity. File within 60 days after service of the legal action; the court may extend for good cause. Filing suspends all discovery until the ruling, except specified and limited discovery the court allows for good cause. (12 O.S. §§ 1431(6), 1432, 1435(B))

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Hearing within 60 days, ruling within 30
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Hearing within 60 days, ruling within 30: The hearing must be set within 60 days after service of the motion, never later than 90 days (120 days if limited discovery is allowed). The court must rule within 30 days after the hearing, considering the pleadings and affidavits. On request of the movant, it must also issue findings within 30 days on whether the suit was brought to deter protected activity or for an improper purpose. (12 O.S. §§ 1433, 1434(A), 1435(A), 1436)

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Burden shifting
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Burden shifting: The movant must show by a preponderance that the action is based on, relates to, or responds to protected activity. The claimant then avoids dismissal only by establishing by clear and specific evidence a prima facie case for each essential element. Even so, the court must dismiss if the movant proves each element of a valid defense by a preponderance. (12 O.S. § 1434(B)-(D))

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Mandatory fees and sanctions
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Mandatory fees and sanctions: On dismissal, the court must award the movant costs, reasonable attorney fees, and other expenses as justice and equity require, and must sanction the claimant enough to deter similar suits. If the motion is frivolous or solely for delay, the court may award the respondent costs and fees. (12 O.S. § 1438)

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Appeal: denial by inaction is appealable and expedited
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Appeal: denial by inaction is appealable and expedited: If the court does not rule within the 30 days, the motion is denied by operation of law and the movant may appeal. Appellate courts must expedite appeals and writs from orders on the motion or failure to rule. (12 O.S. § 1437)

docs.t: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP — Exemptions
docs.x: Oklahoma anti-SLAPP. Exemptions: Does not apply to enforcement actions by the Attorney General or a district attorney; claims against sellers or lessors over statements arising from sales or leases of goods, services, or insurance aimed at actual or potential customers; bodily injury, wrongful death, or survival claims (and statements about them); Insurance Code or insurance-contract claims; and claims from officer-director, employment, or independent-contractor relationships for misappropriating trade secrets or corporate opportunities or enforcing non-disparagement, noncompete, nondisclosure, or confidentiality agreements. (12 O.S. § 1439 (as amended by Laws 2025, c. 180, eff. Nov. 1, 2025))

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — Petition in error (appeal from final judgment)
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. Petition in error (appeal from final judgment): 30 days from Filing of the written, signed judgment conforming to § 696.3 with the trial court clerk (or earliest record date of mailing to the appellant if not mailed within 3 days) (12 O.S. § 990A(A)). Jurisdictional. Filed with the Clerk of the Supreme Court; mailing date by postmark counts.

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — Appeal after timely post-trial motion
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. Appeal after timely post-trial motion: 30 days from Filing of the order disposing of a new-trial, JNOV, or correct/open/modify/vacate/reconsider motion filed within 10 days of judgment (12 O.S. § 990.2(A)). No appeal may be commenced while such a motion is pending. Fee and cost motions do not count.

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — Motion for new trial
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. Motion for new trial: 10 days from Filing of the conforming judgment (12 O.S. § 653(A)). Later relief only by petition under § 655. Extended from the record mailing date if the judgment was not mailed within 3 days.

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — Motion to correct, open, modify, or vacate
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. Motion to correct, open, modify, or vacate: 30 days from Filing of the conforming judgment (12 O.S. § 1031.1(B)). Only a motion filed within 10 days suspends appeal time (§ 990.2). After 30 days, use a petition under § 1033.

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — Interlocutory appeal by right (injunction, receiver, class certification, new trial granted, etc.)
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. Interlocutory appeal by right (injunction, receiver, class certification, new trial granted, etc.): 30 days from Filing of the conforming order (12 O.S. § 993(A)). Petition in error AND record due within the 30 days; the Supreme Court may extend time for the record for good cause.

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — New petition after dismissal as premature
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. New petition after dismissal as premature: 30 days from Mailing of notice that the appeal was dismissed as premature (or the regular period, whichever is later) (12 O.S. § 990A(F)(2)).

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — Service of filed judgment on all parties
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. Service of filed judgment on all parties: 3 days from Filing of the judgment (12 O.S. § 696.2(B)). Duty of the preparing party; a certificate of service must be filed.

docs.t: Oklahoma appeal deadline — OCPA ruling (else denied by operation of law, appealable)
docs.x: Oklahoma appellate deadline. OCPA ruling (else denied by operation of law, appealable): 30 days from Hearing on the anti-SLAPP motion (12 O.S. §§ 1434(A), 1437(A)). Appeal is expedited.

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Confidential Information Form and certification on every filing
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Confidential Information Form and certification on every filing: Every filing in the trial and appellate courts must certify compliance with the Case Records Public Access Policy. Social Security numbers, financial account numbers (other than the last four digits where needed), driver license and SID numbers, minors’ names and birth dates, and abuse victims’ contact information in family cases go only on a contemporaneously filed Confidential Information Form. The court is not required to redact; compliance is solely the filer’s responsibility. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 205.6; Pa.R.A.P. 127; 204 Pa. Code § 213.81, Policy § 7.0)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Preliminary objections, not motions to dismiss; some defenses only as new matter
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Preliminary objections, not motions to dismiss; some defenses only as new matter: Rule 12-type challenges are raised by preliminary objections, and all of them must be raised at once. The statute of limitations and statute of frauds cannot be raised by preliminary objection and must be pleaded as new matter. Improper venue is waived if not raised by preliminary objection. A complaint can be amended as of course within 20 days after service of the objections. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 1028, 1030, 1006)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — A general denial is an admission
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. A general denial is an admission: Every averment that requires a response is admitted unless specifically denied. A general denial or demand for proof counts as an admission. Lack of knowledge works as a denial only after a stated reasonable investigation. New matter endorsed with a notice to plead must be answered within 20 days or it is admitted. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 1026, 1029)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Serve within 30 days in state (90 out of state), or reissue
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Serve within 30 days in state (90 out of state), or reissue: Original process must be served within 30 days in Pennsylvania and 90 days outside it. If not served in time, it must be reissued or reinstated by praecipe, and the plaintiff must make a good-faith effort to serve, or the filing may not stop the statute of limitations (see the Rule 405 citation to Lamp v. Heyman). (Pa.R.Civ.P. 401, 404)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Ten-day notice before default or non pros, every time
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Ten-day notice before default or non pros, every time: The prothonotary cannot enter a default judgment or judgment of non pros by praecipe unless the praecipe certifies that written notice of intent was mailed or delivered at least 10 days earlier, with a copy attached. The notice cannot be waived. For default, it must go to the defaulting party and its counsel. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 237.1, 237.5)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Certificate of merit within 60 days in professional liability cases
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Certificate of merit within 60 days in professional liability cases: Any claim that a licensed professional deviated from professional standards needs a certificate of merit for each professional defendant, filed with the complaint or within 60 days. After a defendant’s notice of intent (no earlier than day 31), a missing certificate leads to judgment of non pros 30 days later. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 1042.3, 1042.6, 1042.7)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Pro hac vice motion 3 days before appearing, after paying IOLTA
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Pro hac vice motion 3 days before appearing, after paying IOLTA: The $375 IOLTA fee per case and the information filing must come first. The sponsor’s Rule 1012.1 motion, with both verified statements and the IOLTA fee certification or averment, must be filed at least 3 days before the out-of-state lawyer appears. The sponsor remains attorney of record. (Pa.B.A.R. 301(b); 204 Pa. Code §§ 81.503(d), 81.505; Pa.R.Civ.P. 1012.1)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Post-trial motion within 10 days, then enter judgment
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Post-trial motion within 10 days, then enter judgment: After any civil trial, grounds not raised at trial and specifically stated in a Rule 227.1 motion filed within 10 days are waived on appeal. The appeal runs from the judgment entered on praecipe, not from the order denying post-trial relief. If the motions are undecided after 120 days, a party may have judgment entered. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 227.1, 227.4)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Rule 1925(b) Statement: omit an issue and it is gone
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Rule 1925(b) Statement: omit an issue and it is gone: If the trial judge orders a concise Statement of errors, file it of record and serve it on the judge within the time ordered (at least 21 days). Every issue not included is waived. The appeal clock is 30 days, is not tolled by a reconsideration motion unless reconsideration is expressly granted within that time, and cannot be extended. (Pa.R.A.P. 1925(b), 1701(b)(3), 903(a), 105(b))

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Document subpoenas to non-parties need 20 days’ notice first
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Document subpoenas to non-parties need 20 days’ notice first: Before serving a subpoena for documents on a non-party, give every party 20 days’ written notice with the proposed subpoena. An objection blocks service until the court rules. Federal-style same-day service of notice and subpoena will not work. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 4009.21-4009.24)

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Check county local rules before filing anything
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Check county local rules before filing anything: Motion procedure, briefing, argument lists, preliminary objection and summary judgment practice, e-filing availability, cover sheets and the compulsory arbitration limit all vary by county. Each county also designates the office listed in the notice to defend. Read the county’s published local rules (Pa.R.J.A. 103(d)) before the first filing. (Pa.R.Civ.P. 239-239.9, 1018.1(c), 1301; Pa.R.J.A. 103(d))

docs.t: Pennsylvania — Anti-SLAPP special motion: confirm it is in force, and file within 60 days
docs.x: Pennsylvania land mine. Anti-SLAPP special motion: confirm it is in force, and file within 60 days: UPEPA immunity and mandatory fee awards apply to actions filed after July 17, 2024. The special-motion procedure in § 8340.16 (60-day deadline, automatic stay) depends on a Pennsylvania Bulletin notice that this research could not confirm. Plead immunity in preliminary objections, new matter or summary judgment as well, and file any special motion within 60 days of service. (42 Pa.C.S. §§ 8340.15-8340.18; Act 72 of 2024, §§ 3, 6, 7)

docs.t: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP — Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (2024): immunity and fees
docs.x: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP. Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (2024): immunity and fees: Act 72 of 2024 (signed July 17, 2024) added 42 Pa.C.S. §§ 8340.11-8340.18. A person is immune from civil liability for a cause of action based on protected public expression if the claimant fails to establish a prima facie case on each element, or fails to state a claim, or if there is no genuine issue of material fact and the defendant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. ‘Protected public expression’ means communication in, or on an issue under review in, a legislative, executive, judicial or administrative proceeding. It also covers exercising, on a matter of public concern, the freedoms of speech, press, assembly, petition or association protected by the First Amendment or Pa. Const. art. I, §§ 7 or 20. The statute must be broadly construed. (42 Pa.C.S. §§ 8340.12-8340.13, 8340.15; Act

docs.t: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP — What UPEPA does not cover
docs.x: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP. What UPEPA does not cover: The Act excludes claims against, or enforcement claims by, government units and officials acting officially. It also excludes claims against a business arising from communications about its own goods or services (creative and journalistic works are not ‘goods or services’), and bodily injury and death claims unless they sound in defamation, privacy, misappropriation of likeness or emotional distress, or arise solely from public-concern speech. Further exclusions: protection-from-abuse and sexual-violence protection cases; insurance law and insurance-contract claims; trade-secret and corporate-opportunity misappropriation; enforcing nondisparagement or noncompete agreements against a party to them; internal business governance disputes; and manager liability or indemnity. It applies to civil actions commenced, and causes of action assert

docs.t: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP — Special motion: 60 days, automatic stay, quick hearing
docs.x: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP. Special motion: 60 days, automatic stay, quick hearing: A party may file a special motion to dismiss, or for judgment on, all or part of a claim based on protected public expression immunity. It is due no later than 60 days after service of the pleading asserting the claim, extendable for good cause. The court hears argument within 60 days after filing and rules, with a written opinion, within 60 days after argument. It decides on the summary-judgment record (Pa.R.Civ.P. 1035.1-1035.2). Filing stays all other proceedings, including discovery and the duty to file a responsive pleading, until the order is final, including any appeal. During the stay, parties may still challenge service, jurisdiction or venue, and may voluntarily discontinue. The court may allow limited discovery needed to resolve immunity and may hear urgent public-safety injunction requests. The r

docs.t: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP — Fees and immediate appeal
docs.x: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP. Fees and immediate appeal: If the defendant is immune, the court must award attorney fees, court costs and litigation expenses, jointly and severally against each adverse party that asserted the claim. It must do the same if the claimant voluntarily discontinues (with or without prejudice) after immunity is asserted. If the immunity assertion is frivolous or solely for delay, the court must award the opposing party its fees incurred in opposing it. An order granting, denying or otherwise determining immunity is immediately appealable under 42 Pa.C.S. § 702. A separate cause of action lets a person recover fees and costs of the underlying case if that person would have prevailed on immunity but the court never ruled on it. Punitive damages are available on proof that the underlying suit was brought or continued solely to harass, intimidate, punish or maliciously i

docs.t: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP — Older environmental anti-SLAPP law still applies
docs.x: Pennsylvania anti-SLAPP. Older environmental anti-SLAPP law still applies: A person who files an action to enforce an environmental law, or communicates with a government agency about enforcing or implementing one, is immune from civil liability in a resulting damages action when the action or communication aims to procure favorable government action. The immunity is lost if the allegation or communication is not relevant or material to environmental enforcement or implementation and also is knowingly false or reckless, is made solely to interfere with business relationships, or is later found to be wrongful use or abuse of process. The defendant may move for a hearing on immunity. If the motion is denied, there is an interlocutory appeal of right to the Commonwealth Court, and discovery is stayed during the appeal. A government agency may intervene or participate as amicus. A successful

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Notice of appeal from a final civil order (filed in the trial court)
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Notice of appeal from a final civil order (filed in the trial court): 30 days from Entry of the order (civil: the date the clerk notes Rule 236 notice on the docket) (Pa.R.A.P. 903(a), 108(b)). Cannot be extended (Pa.R.A.P. 105(b)); late filing invalidates the appeal (Pa.R.A.P. 902(b)(2)).

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Cross-appeal
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Cross-appeal: 14 days from Service of the first notice of appeal (or the original 30 days, whichever is later) (Pa.R.A.P. 903(b)). Identify it as a cross-appeal.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Appeal in Election Code, Local Government Unit Debt Act, or criminal venue/venire matters
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Appeal in Election Code, Local Government Unit Debt Act, or criminal venue/venire matters: 10 days from Entry of the order (Pa.R.A.P. 903(c)(1)). The Supreme Court has shortened Election Code periods by order for specific elections.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Election that an order sustaining venue or jurisdiction is final
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Election that an order sustaining venue or jurisdiction is final: 10 days from Entry of the order (Pa.R.A.P. 311(b)(1)). Filed by the party benefiting from the order. The notice of appeal is then due 30 days after the election (Pa.R.A.P. 903(c)(2)).

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Motion for post-trial relief (civil)
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Motion for post-trial relief (civil): 10 days from Verdict, discharge of jury, or nonsuit (jury); notice of nonsuit or filing of decision (non-jury) (Pa.R.Civ.P. 227.1(c)). Other parties: 10 days after the first motion is filed. Issues not raised are waived.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Judgment on praecipe if post-trial motions are undecided
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Judgment on praecipe if post-trial motions are undecided: 120 days from Filing of the first post-trial motion (Pa.R.Civ.P. 227.4(1)(b)). A judgment entered this way is final and not subject to reconsideration.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Application for a Rule 341(c) determination of finality
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Application for a Rule 341(c) determination of finality: 30 days from Entry of the order (Pa.R.A.P. 341(c)(1)-(2)). Deemed denied if the trial court does not act within 30 days of filing. Notice of appeal is due within 30 days of the amended order.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Application to amend an interlocutory order to add § 702(b) certification
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Application to amend an interlocutory order to add § 702(b) certification: 30 days from Entry of the interlocutory order (Pa.R.A.P. 1311(b)). Deemed denied after 30 days without action.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Petition for permission to appeal (interlocutory)
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Petition for permission to appeal (interlocutory): 30 days from Entry of the amended (certified) order, or the denial or deemed denial of certification (Pa.R.A.P. 1311(b)). Filed with the appellate prothonotary. Cannot be extended (Pa.R.A.P. 105(b)).

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Rule 1925(b) Statement of errors
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Rule 1925(b) Statement of errors: 21 days from Entry on the docket of the trial judge’s order (minimum; the order sets the actual number of days) (Pa.R.A.P. 1925(b)(2)(i), (b)(3)(i)). Issues omitted are waived. Must be filed of record and served on the judge.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Transmission of record to appellate court
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Transmission of record to appellate court: 60 days from Filing of the notice of appeal (Pa.R.A.P. 1931(a)(1)). Extended if a Rule 1925(b)(2) extension is granted.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Designation of reproduced record
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Designation of reproduced record: 30 days from Before the appellant’s brief is due (Pa.R.A.P. 2154(a)). Appellee may counter-designate within 10 days after receiving it.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 40 days from Filing of the record (unless the prothonotary fixes another date) (Pa.R.A.P. 2185(a)(1)). Children’s fast track appeals: 30 days.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 30 days from Service of the appellant’s brief and reproduced record (Pa.R.A.P. 2185(a)(1)). Children’s fast track appeals: 21 days.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Reply brief: 14 days from Service of the preceding brief (Pa.R.A.P. 2185(a)(1)). Must also be received at least 3 days before argument.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Application for reargument
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Application for reargument: 14 days from Entry of the appellate judgment or order (Pa.R.A.P. 2542(a)(1)). Children’s fast track: 7 days. Limit 3,000 words.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Petition for allowance of appeal to the Supreme Court
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Petition for allowance of appeal to the Supreme Court: 30 days from Entry of the Superior or Commonwealth Court order (or of the order disposing of a timely reargument application) (Pa.R.A.P. 1113(a)). Cannot be extended (Pa.R.A.P. 105(b)). Limit 9,000 words.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Cross-petition for allowance of appeal
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Cross-petition for allowance of appeal: 14 days from Service of the first petition (Pa.R.A.P. 1113(b)). Or within the original 30 days, whichever is later.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Answer to petition for allowance of appeal
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Answer to petition for allowance of appeal: 14 days from Service of the petition (Pa.R.A.P. 1116(a)). Limit 9,000 words.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Answer to jurisdictional statement (direct Supreme Court appeal)
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Answer to jurisdictional statement (direct Supreme Court appeal): 14 days from Service of the jurisdictional statement (Pa.R.A.P. 909(b)).

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Petition for review of agency (quasi-judicial) order
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Petition for review of agency (quasi-judicial) order: 30 days from Entry of the order (Pa.R.A.P. 1512(a)(1)). Some statutes set 15 days (Pa.R.A.P. 1512(b)). Cannot be extended.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Cross-petition for review
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Cross-petition for review: 14 days from Service of the first petition for review (Pa.R.A.P. 1512(a)(2)). Or within the original 30 days, whichever is later.

docs.t: Pennsylvania appeal deadline — Anti-SLAPP special motion (UPEPA)
docs.x: Pennsylvania appellate deadline. Anti-SLAPP special motion (UPEPA): 60 days from Service of the pleading asserting the claim (42 Pa.C.S. § 8340.16(b)). Extendable for good cause. Effective date of § 8340.16 depends on a Pa. Bulletin notice under Act 72 of 2024 § 3(4); confirm before relying on it.

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Reconsideration: 15 days, two different clocks, and simultaneous service
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Reconsideration: 15 days, two different clocks, and simultaneous service: From an interlocutory order or resolution: 15 days from notice, a strict-compliance term. From a judgment: 15 days from archivo en autos of the notice, a jurisdictional term that cannot be extended. The motion must be served on all parties within the same 15 days, and it must state with particularity the facts and law to reconsider. A motion that lacks that specificity is denied and does not toll the time to appeal. A proper motion tolls the appeal time for all parties. (R. Proc. Civ. 47, 52.2(e)(2), 68.2)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Appeal and certiorari: 30 days, and some cannot be saved
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Appeal and certiorari: 30 days, and some cannot be saved: Civil appeal to the Court of Appeals: 30 days from archivo en autos of the notice of judgment, jurisdictional. Certiorari from interlocutory trial orders: 30 days from notice, strict compliance, extendable only for special circumstances explained in the petition itself. Certiorari to the Supreme Court from Court of Appeals judgments in appeals: 30 days, jurisdictional. The trial court cannot extend the terms in Rules 43.1, 44.1, 47, 48.2, 48.4, 49.2, or 52.2. (R. Proc. Civ. 52.2(a)-(b), 68.2; Reglamento TA R. 13(A), 32(B)-(C))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Court of Appeals: the fee payment date is the filing date
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Court of Appeals: the fee payment date is the filing date: Uploading the appeal to SUMAC is not filing. The filing receipt warns that the document is not officially filed until the filing fees are paid, and the filing date is the fee payment date. It does not relate back to the upload. The 11:59 p.m. e-filing rule also does not apply to filings that require a fee. Pay on the platform the same day. If the trial case has no electronic record, also send the trial court clerk a stamped cover page within 72 hours (strict compliance). (Reglamento TA R. 14(A); Directrices SUMAC §§ VII, XVI(1))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Serve the appellate brief on the other side within the filing period
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Serve the appellate brief on the other side within the filing period: The appellant must serve the appeal and appendices on the other parties within the time to file the appeal (strict compliance) and certify the date of service. E-filing serves lawyers, but pro se parties and others the law requires must be served separately. (Reglamento TA R. 13(B))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Summons must be served within 120 days, or the case is dismissed
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Summons must be served within 120 days, or the case is dismissed: Serve the summons within 120 days of filing the complaint (or of issuance of a summons by publication). If service is not completed in time, the court must dismiss without prejudice. A second dismissal for the same failure operates as an adjudication on the merits. Service cannot be done through SUMAC. Out-of-island defendants may be served personally, under the law of the place of service, by letters rogatory, by publication, or as the court orders. (R. Proc. Civ. 4.3(b)-(c), 67.6)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Nonresident plaintiffs must post a cost bond
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Nonresident plaintiffs must post a cost bond: When the claimant lives outside Puerto Rico or is a foreign corporation, the court must require a bond of at least $1,000 for costs, expenses, and attorney’s fees, and all proceedings are stayed until it is posted. If it is not posted within 60 days of the order, the court dismisses the case. Narrow exceptions apply: indigent litigants exempt from filing fees, co-owners suing over Puerto Rico property alongside a resident co-owner, and partition of property located in Puerto Rico. (R. Proc. Civ. 69.5)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Court of Appeals reconsideration: 15 days, no extensions
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Court of Appeals reconsideration: 15 days, no extensions: A motion to reconsider a Court of Appeals decision, civil or criminal, is due within 15 days of archivo en autos of the notice, and the term cannot be extended. A timely motion stops the clock to go to the Supreme Court, which restarts when notice of the ruling on the motion is filed. (Reglamento TA R. 84(A); R. Proc. Civ. 52.2(f))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Criminal appeals run from the date of sentencing
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Criminal appeals run from the date of sentencing: A criminal appeal is due within 30 days after the sentence is pronounced, not after notice. The term is jurisdictional. A timely new-trial or reconsideration motion restarts the 30 days from notice of the order resolving it. Certiorari from a conviction on a guilty plea is also 30 days from the sentence, jurisdictional. (Reglamento TA R. 23(A), 32(A))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Agency review: 30 days to the Court of Appeals
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Agency review: 30 days to the Court of Appeals: Judicial review of a final agency order or decision goes directly to the Court of Appeals within 30 days (jurisdictional) of archivo en autos of the notice, or of the restarted date after a timely agency reconsideration motion, unless a special law sets a different term. (Reglamento TA R. 57)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Pro hac vice counsel cannot e-file and must bring local counsel everywhere
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Pro hac vice counsel cannot e-file and must bring local counsel everywhere: A courtesy-admitted lawyer has no SUMAC filing access and must file on paper. The endorsing Puerto Rico lawyer must sign every filing and attend every hearing and deposition unless excused. Budget for full local-counsel participation, not a name on the signature block. (Reglamento TS R. 12(f)(2); Directrices SUMAC § V(3))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Withdrawal needs leave of court
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Withdrawal needs leave of court: Counsel who has appeared must move in writing to withdraw, give reasons, provide the client’s phone and mailing address, and certify the client was notified. The court may refuse in exceptional cases if a party’s rights would be seriously harmed or the case unduly delayed. (R. Proc. Civ. 9.2)

docs.t: Puerto Rico anti-SLAPP — Status not confirmed from the collected texts
docs.x: Puerto Rico anti-SLAPP. Status not confirmed from the collected texts: The collected Puerto Rico court texts (civil and criminal procedure, evidence, court rules, ethics rules, e-filing guidelines) contain no anti-SLAPP procedure: no special motion to dismiss, no discovery stay, and no fee-shifting rule tied to speech or petitioning. An anti-SLAPP law, if one exists, would be a statute outside these rules. Before telling a client anything, search the Leyes de Puerto Rico Anotadas (LPRA) and the Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto virtual library (bvirtualogp.pr.gov) for any enacted law on strategic lawsuits against public participation, and confirm its number, effective date, and procedure. No statute is named here because none could be verified. (None verified; check LPRA and enacted laws (Leyes) for any anti-SLAPP statute)

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Civil appeal (apelación) to the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Civil appeal (apelación) to the TA: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of judgment (SUMAC send date; mailing date if later) (Regla 13(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(a) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. Restarts after a timely Rule 43.1, 47 or 48 motion is decided and notified.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Civil appeal to the TA when the government is a party
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Civil appeal to the TA when the government is a party: 60 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of judgment (Regla 13(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(c) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. Applies to any aggrieved party when the ELA, its officials, a non-public-corporation instrumentality, or a municipality or its officials is a party.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TA against interlocutory orders (civil or criminal), protection orders, and judgments on arb
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TA against interlocutory orders (civil or criminal), protection orders, and judgments on arbitration-award review: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the order (Civ. Rule 52.2(b) says “fecha de notificación”) (Regla 32(C) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Strict compliance: excusable only for special circumstances explained in the petition. No 60-day government extension.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TA against final resolutions in jurisdicción voluntaria
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TA against final resolutions in jurisdicción voluntaria: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the resolution (Regla 32(B) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional, unless a special law sets another term.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TA against a guilty-plea conviction
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TA against a guilty-plea conviction: 30 days from Date the sentence was dictated (mailing date of notice if the defendant was not present) (Regla 32(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 193 R. Proc. Crim.). Jurisdictional. Criminal rules compilation current only to Feb. 2020.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Criminal appeal to the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Criminal appeal to the TA: 30 days from Date the sentence was dictated; or notice of the order denying a timely new-trial motion (Rules 188(e), 192) or deciding a timely reconsideration (Regla 23(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 194 R. Proc. Crim.). Jurisdictional. Regla 23 counts from notice to the accused of the ruling; Rule 194 counts a reconsideration ruling from its archivo en autos. Criminal rules compilation current only to Feb. 2020.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Recurso de revisión (final agency decision) to the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Recurso de revisión (final agency decision) to the TA: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the final order (mailing date if later), or the applicable date after a timely reconsideration (Regla 57 Reglamento TA). Jurisdictional unless a special law provides otherwise. Agency reconsideration terms are in the LPAU, not reviewed here.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Recurso de revisión especial (welfare benefits, pro se)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Recurso de revisión especial (welfare benefits, pro se): 30 days from Receipt of the agency’s final order (Regla 67(C) Reglamento TA). Only for self-represented persons challenging welfare-benefit decisions.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Electoral certiorari to the TA (CEE cases)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Electoral certiorari to the TA (CEE cases): 10 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TPI judgment (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 42 Reglamento TA). Jurisdictional. Within 30 days before an election: 48 hours. Within 5 days before: 24 hours, with same-day notice. No reconsideration in those windows.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Serve the recurso and appendix on the other parties (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Serve the recurso and appendix on the other parties (TA): Within the filing term days from Same trigger as the recurso (Reglas 13(B)(1), 23(B), 33(B) y 58(B)(1) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance. E-filing serves counsel; you must serve self-represented and other required parties.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Notify the TPI when its case has no electronic record
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Notify the TPI when its case has no electronic record: 72 hours (civil appeal); 48 hours (criminal appeal, certiorari) days from Filing of the recurso (Reglas 14(A), 24(A) y 33(A) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance. Not needed when SUMAC posts the entry automatically in an electronic TPI record.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Send the original to the TA after filing on paper at the TPI
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Send the original to the TA after filing on paper at the TPI: 48 hours days from Filing at the TPI Secretaría (Reglas 14(C), 24(B) y 33(A) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance. Only when paper filing is allowed under Regla 2.1.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Supplementary certification of service
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Supplementary certification of service: 48 hours (3 business days in revisión) days from Filing of the recurso (Reglas 15 y 58(B)(4) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Late appendix documents, with leave
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Late appendix documents, with leave: 15 days from Notice of the TA resolution allowing late filing (Reglas 16(E)(2) y 34(E)(2) Reglamento TA). Failure to cure may lead to dismissal.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Notice of intent to reproduce oral evidence
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Notice of intent to reproduce oral evidence: 10 days from Filing of the recurso (Reglas 19(B), 29(B) y 76(A) Reglamento TA). Identify portions, dates and witnesses, and the method proposed.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Motion in the TPI or agency for the re-recording (regrabación)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Motion in the TPI or agency for the re-recording (regrabación): 10 days from Notice of the TA order authorizing reproduction (Regla 76(B) Reglamento TA). Pay the fees with the motion.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Transcript of oral evidence
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Transcript of oral evidence: 30 days from Delivery of the re-recording (Regla 76(C) Reglamento TA). Or the term the TA orders; extendable only for good cause by a reasoned motion. Serve copies within the same term.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Stipulated narrative statement: draft, then negotiation
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Stipulated narrative statement: draft, then negotiation: 30, then 20 days from TA authorization; then service of the draft (Regla 76(D) Reglamento TA). If no agreement, the other side files specific objections.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Supplementary brief after transcript or narrative (civil appeal)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Supplementary brief after transcript or narrative (civil appeal): 30 days from Filing of the transcript or narrative statement (Regla 21 Reglamento TA). Announce it when filing the transcript. The appellee may reply within 30 days.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief, civil appeal (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief, civil appeal (TA): 30 days from Filing of the escrito de apelación; or filing of the reproduced oral evidence if any is brought up (Regla 22 Reglamento TA). May include its own appendix.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Opposition to certiorari (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Opposition to certiorari (TA): 10 days from Notification of the petition (Regla 37(A) Reglamento TA). 25 pages paper / 35 electronic.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Respondent’s brief after the TA issues certiorari
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Respondent’s brief after the TA issues certiorari: 30 days from Notice of issuance of the writ (Regla 39(A) Reglamento TA). Extendable. The petition is the petitioner’s brief.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Opposition brief in administrative revisión
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Opposition brief in administrative revisión: 30 days from Notification of the recurso (Regla 63(A) Reglamento TA). Due from the agency, the official and other parties.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Criminal appellant’s brief; then El Pueblo’s brief
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Criminal appellant’s brief; then El Pueblo’s brief: 30, then 30 days from Elevation of the record; then filing of the appellant’s brief (Regla 28(A), (E) Reglamento TA). Unless the TA orders otherwise.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Response to a motion (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Response to a motion (TA): 10 days from Notification of the motion (Regla 68(B) Reglamento TA). The TA may rule sooner in extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Request for an extension (TA or TS)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Request for an extension (TA or TS): At least 3 business days before the term expires days from Expiration of the term (Regla 72(B) Reglamento TA; Regla 48(b) Reglamento TS). Never available for jurisdictional terms.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Panel review of a single judge’s habeas corpus or mandamus resolution
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Panel review of a single judge’s habeas corpus or mandamus resolution: 10 days from Archivo en autos of the notice of the resolution (Regla 55(H) Reglamento TA).

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration of a TPI civil judgment
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration of a TPI civil judgment: 15 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of judgment (Regla 47 R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. Serve the other parties within the same 15 days (strict compliance). Must be specific or it does not interrupt.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration of a TPI interlocutory order
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration of a TPI interlocutory order: 15 days from Notice of the order (Regla 47 R. Proc. Civ.). Strict compliance.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration of a criminal sentence or conviction (TPI)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration of a criminal sentence or conviction (TPI): 15 days from Date the sentence was dictated (Regla 194 R. Proc. Crim.). Not extendable. Criminal rules compilation current only to Feb. 2020.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration in the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration in the TA: 15 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TA decision (Regla 84(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 216 R. Proc. Crim.). Not extendable. Suspends the term to go to the TS. Opposition within 10 days. Electoral cases: 10 days under Regla 42.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TS against a TA judgment in an appeal
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TS against a TA judgment in an appeal: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice (or of the ruling on reconsideration; mailing date if later) (Regla 20(a)(1), (c) Reglamento TS; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. 60 days in civil cases where the government is a party.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TS against TA rulings on guilty-plea certiorari, jurisdicción voluntaria, or administrative
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TS against TA rulings on guilty-plea certiorari, jurisdicción voluntaria, or administrative revisión: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 20(a)(2), (3), (5) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TS against other TA rulings in discretionary recursos, or TA interlocutory resolutions
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TS against other TA rulings in discretionary recursos, or TA interlocutory resolutions: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice (Civ. Rule 52.2(b) says “fecha de notificación”) (Regla 20(b)(1) Reglamento TS; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Strict compliance. In criminal cases, Rule 217 R. Proc. Crim. calls the 30-day term for certiorari against a TA judgment or final resolution denying certiorari jurisdictional; treat it as jurisdictional.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Direct appeal to the TS (unconstitutionality or conflicting TA decisions)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Direct appeal to the TS (unconstitutionality or conflicting TA decisions): 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TA judgment (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 17(a) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional. 60 days in civil cases where the government is a party.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Notify the TA of a recurso filed in the TS
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Notify the TA of a recurso filed in the TS: 72 hours days from Filing in the TS (Reglas 17(b) y 20(d) Reglamento TS). Strict compliance. Stamped copy without the appendix.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Opposition to certiorari (TS)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Opposition to certiorari (TS): 10 days from Notification of the petition (Regla 20(l) Reglamento TS). 25 pages.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Briefs in the TS after the writ issues or the appeal is accepted
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Briefs in the TS after the writ issues or the appeal is accepted: 30, then 30 days from Receipt of the Secretaría’s notice that the record was received (Regla 35(c)); then receipt of the petitioner’s or appellant’s brief (Reglas 19, 21 y 33(i) Reglamento TS). Regla 33(i) counts the second 30 days from filing of the other side’s brief; Reglas 19 and 21 from receipt. Use the earlier date.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration in the TS
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration in the TS: 10 business days days from Date the decision was sent to the parties (Regla 45(a)–(b) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional; 10 pages; no extensions. A second motion only within 3 business days after notice of the denial.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Electoral certiorari to the TS
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Electoral certiorari to the TS: 10 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TA judgment (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 22(a) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional. Reconsideration within 3 days. The TS rule still cites the 2011 Electoral Code; the Reglamento TA (Regla 41) refers to it as “Regla 21” of the Reglamento TS.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — TA mandate to the TPI or agency
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. TA mandate to the TPI or agency: 10 business days days from The TA decision becoming final and firm (Regla 84(E) Reglamento TA). Since 2025 the TA may send it earlier for cause.

docs.t: Rhode Island — 20 days to appeal, and the Supreme Court cannot extend it
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. 20 days to appeal, and the Supreme Court cannot extend it: A civil notice of appeal, with the $150 filing fee, must be filed in the trial court within 20 days of entry of the judgment, order, or decree (not 30). Only the trial court may extend, for excusable neglect, by no more than 30 days past the original deadline; the Supreme Court has no power to extend the time to appeal. (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a), 20(b))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Post-trial motions are due in 10 days, and only some stop the appeal clock
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Post-trial motions are due in 10 days, and only some stop the appeal clock: Renewed motions for judgment as a matter of law, motions to amend findings, new-trial motions, and motions to alter or amend must be served within 10 days after entry of judgment, and the time cannot be extended. Only those four motions restart the 20-day appeal period. A Rule 60(b) motion does not. (Super.R.Civ.P. 6(b), 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e); Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a))

docs.t: Rhode Island — District Court civil appeals: 2 business days
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. District Court civil appeals: 2 business days: To get a de novo trial in Superior Court after a District Court civil judgment, a party must file a written claim of appeal with the District Court clerk within 2 days after entry of judgment, excluding weekends and legal holidays, and pay the costs, including a $50 attorney’s fee for the other side, at that time. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-12-10)

docs.t: Rhode Island — 12% interest from accrual changes settlement math
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. 12% interest from accrual changes settlement math: Prejudgment interest at 12% a year runs from the date the cause of action accrued and is added by the clerk; post-judgment interest is also 12%, accruing on the prejudgment interest as well. Each year between accrual and judgment adds about 12% of the damages award. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-21-10(a))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Arbitration certificate within 3 days and a 30-day rejection window
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Arbitration certificate within 3 days and a 30-day rejection window: Money cases of $100,000 or less are diverted to court-annexed arbitration. Counsel must file the arbitration certificate within 3 days after the last responsive pleading. Missing the 30-day deadline to file a written rejection (with $300) after the award is filed means judgment enters on the award. (Super. Ct. R. Governing Arbitration of Civil Actions 1(a), (e), 5)

docs.t: Rhode Island — Pro hac vice: 3 cases per 5 years, and local counsel in the room
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Pro hac vice: 3 cases per 5 years, and local counsel in the room: Nonresident lawyers are limited to 3 Rhode Island pro hac vice cases in 5 years unless the Supreme Court waives it, and admission is for ‘special and infrequent’ occasions based on client need. Rhode Island counsel must sign every paper and attend every hearing and trial day, ready to proceed alone, unless excused. (Sup. Ct. Art. II, R. 9(a); Super.R.Civ.P. 85)

docs.t: Rhode Island — Slander has a 1-year statute of limitations
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Slander has a 1-year statute of limitations: Claims for words spoken must be filed within 1 year after the words were spoken. Personal-injury claims get 3 years. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-14(a)-(b))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Uncontested-motion trap: object 3 days before the hearing
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Uncontested-motion trap: object 3 days before the hearing: Motions to amend, compel, for protective orders, to consolidate, to add third parties, for Rule 35 exams, to enlarge time after a deadline, and to assign are granted as a matter of course and never reach the calendar unless a written objection stating particular grounds is served and filed at least 3 days before the hearing. The extra day for electronic service does not apply. (Super.R.Civ.P. 7(b)(3))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Discovery runs on Rhode Island numbers, not federal ones
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Discovery runs on Rhode Island numbers, not federal ones: No initial disclosures. Interrogatory answers and document responses are due in 40 days (a defendant gets 60 days after service of process for document requests), with a 30-interrogatory cap. A plaintiff needs leave to serve interrogatories within 60 days after service of process. Untimely interrogatory objections are waived. Supplemental interrogatory answers are due no later than 30 days before trial. An order compelling discovery can provide for automatic dismissal or default if not obeyed within 30 days. (Super.R.Civ.P. 26, 33(a)-(c), 34(b)(2), 37(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Do not plead a dollar amount in injury cases
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Do not plead a dollar amount in injury cases: In actions for personal injury, property damage, or wrongful death, the complaint must not state the amount claimed, only that it is enough for the court’s jurisdiction. (Super.R.Civ.P. 8(a))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Miss the Rule 12A statement and the appeal is conditionally dismissed
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Miss the Rule 12A statement and the appeal is conditionally dismissed: The Rule 12A statement is due 20 days after the appeal is docketed. If it is late, the Clerk enters a conditional dismissal that becomes final unless the statement or an extension motion is filed within 10 days. A late appellee counter-statement or brief leads to a conditional default barring further filings and argument. (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12A(1)-(2), 18A)

docs.t: Rhode Island — Supreme Court briefs need 9 paper copies within 5 days
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Supreme Court briefs need 9 paper copies within 5 days: Even with mandatory e-filing, parties must deliver 9 paper copies of Rule 12A statements and briefs (6 of appendices, writ petitions, reargument petitions, and supporting memoranda) within 5 days after the Clerk accepts the electronic filing. Briefs must be in 14-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, with a signed word-count certification and the Clerk’s ‘Checklist for Filing Briefs’; a brief without the checklist is rejected. (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 16(f), 18(b), (h))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Statute: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 9-33 (conditional immunity, not a dismissal framework)
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Statute: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 9-33 (conditional immunity, not a dismissal framework): Rhode Island’s 1993 anti-SLAPP law makes a party’s exercise of the right of petition or free speech, under the U.S. or Rhode Island constitutions, in connection with a matter of public concern, conditionally immune from civil claims, counterclaims, and cross-claims directed at that activity. Covered activity is defined as any written or oral statement (1) made before or submitted to a legislative, executive, or judicial body or other governmental proceeding, (2) made in connection with an issue under consideration by such a body, or (3) made in connection with an issue of public concern. The legislative findings say such suits should be resolved quickly and at minimum cost to the citizen. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-1, 9-33-2(a), (e))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — The only exception: ‘sham’ petitioning or speech, tested two ways
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. The only exception: ‘sham’ petitioning or speech, tested two ways: Immunity is lost only if the speech or petition is a sham, meaning it is not genuinely aimed at procuring a favorable government action, result, or outcome. It is a sham only if it is BOTH objectively baseless (no reasonable person could realistically expect success in procuring the government action) AND subjectively baseless (an attempt to use the governmental process itself, rather than its outcome, for its own direct effects). The statute’s sham test is framed around petitioning government. How it applies to speech on a public issue that is not aimed at any government body is not answered by the statutory text; check Rhode Island case law. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-33-2(a)(1)-(2))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Procedure: no special motion form, no deadline, automatic discovery stay
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Procedure: no special motion form, no deadline, automatic discovery stay: Immunity may be raised by an appropriate motion or by other appropriate means under the civil rules. The statute sets no filing deadline and no hearing deadline. Filing a motion asserting the immunity automatically stays all discovery until notice of entry of the order ruling on it. The court may allow specified discovery only on motion, after a hearing, for good cause. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-33-2(b)-(c))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Fees are mandatory for the winner; damages if the suit was frivolous or meant to harass
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Fees are mandatory for the winner; damages if the suit was frivolous or meant to harass: If the court grants the immunity motion, or the speaker or petitioner ultimately prevails at trial, the court must award costs and reasonable attorney’s fees, including those for the motion and related discovery. The court must also award compensatory damages, and may award punitive damages, if the prevailing party shows the claims were frivolous or brought to harass or otherwise inhibit petitioning or speech. Other remedies remain available. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-33-2(d))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Intervention by government and the Attorney General; other protections preserved
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Intervention by government and the Attorney General; other protections preserved: The government agency or subdivision to which the petition or speech was directed, or the Attorney General, may intervene to defend or support the speaker. The chapter does not limit other constitutional, statutory, or common-law protections. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-3, 9-33-4)

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Appeal of a denial: the statute is silent
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Appeal of a denial: the statute is silent: Chapter 9-33 has no appeal provision, and a denial of an immunity motion is not among the interlocutory orders made appealable by R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-24-7 (injunctions, receivers, ordered sales, and new-trial orders after a jury trial). Review before final judgment would have to come by petition for certiorari to the Supreme Court under Article I, Rule 13. Whether the Supreme Court routinely grants such review is a case-law question not answered by the collected texts. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-2, 9-24-7; Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 13)

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Currency check
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Currency check: The legislature’s site shows § 9-33-2 last amended by P.L. 1995, ch. 386, and § 9-33-4 by P.L. 1997, ch. 326. No later amendment (for example, adoption of the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act) appears on the official code site as fetched November 10, 2026. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-1 to 9-33-4 (History of Section notes))

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Notice of appeal, civil (with $150 fee)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Notice of appeal, civil (with $150 fee): 20 days from Entry of the judgment, order, or decree (set forth and signed by the clerk) (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a), 5(a)). Filed in the trial court. Restarts from entry of an order deciding a timely Rule 50(b), 52(b), or 59 motion. The Supreme Court cannot extend it.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Cross-appeal / other party’s notice of appeal
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Cross-appeal / other party’s notice of appeal: 20 days from Filing (or deemed filing) of the first notice of appeal, or the ordinary appeal period if longer (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a)). Whichever period ends later.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Extension of appeal time for excusable neglect
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Extension of appeal time for excusable neglect: 30 days from Expiration of the original appeal period (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a)). Granted only by the trial court; maximum 30 days.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Rule 50(b), 52(b), or 59 post-trial motion (tolls the appeal period)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Rule 50(b), 52(b), or 59 post-trial motion (tolls the appeal period): 10 days from Entry of judgment (Super.R.Civ.P. 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e); Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a)). Cannot be extended (Super.R.Civ.P. 6(b)). Rule 60(b) motions do not toll.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Order transcript (and file statement of parts and points if partial)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Order transcript (and file statement of parts and points if partial): 20 days from Filing of the notice of appeal (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 10(b)(1)). 60 days from the notice of appeal for mediation-eligible civil appeals (R. 35(e)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Transmit record to the Supreme Court
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Transmit record to the Supreme Court: 60 days from Filing of the notice of appeal (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 11(a), (c)). Trial court may extend to no more than 90 days from the first notice of appeal. Mediation cases: 60 days from ordering the transcript (R. 35(e)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Mediation Statement (Parts I and II)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Mediation Statement (Parts I and II): 20 days from Date of the Notice of Eligibility (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 35(d)(1)-(2)). Part II is confidential and goes only to the mediation program.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Report errors in docketed case title
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Report errors in docketed case title: 7 days from Notice of docketing (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12(b)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Motion to correct the record
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Motion to correct the record: 20 days from Docketing (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12(d)). Or further time the Court allows.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Rule 12A statement of the case (3,000 words)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Rule 12A statement of the case (3,000 words): 20 days from Docketing of the appeal (or receipt of the record on granted certiorari) (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12A(1)). Must attach the judgment and the trial court’s decision. Late filing leads to conditional dismissal (R. 18A(1)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Rule 12A counter-statement (3,000 words)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Rule 12A counter-statement (3,000 words): 15 days from Filing of the appellant’s statement (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12A(2)). Late filing leads to conditional default (R. 18A(2)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Show cause supplemental statement (3,000 words)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Show cause supplemental statement (3,000 words): 20 days from Issuance of the show cause order (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12A(4)). Responding party’s counter-statement 10 days after that statement is filed or was due.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief (15,000 words)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief (15,000 words): 40 days from Clerk’s notice of assignment to the regular calendar for full briefing (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 16(a), (f)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief (15,000 words)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief (15,000 words): 40 days from Filing of the appellant’s brief (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 16(b), (f)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Reply brief (7,500 words)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Reply brief (7,500 words): 20 days from Filing of the appellee’s brief (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 16(c), (f)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Paper copies of Rule 12A statements and briefs (9) or appendices, petitions, memoranda (6)
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Paper copies of Rule 12A statements and briefs (9) or appendices, petitions, memoranda (6): 5 days from Clerk’s acceptance of the electronic filing (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 18(h)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Correct and resubmit a rejected filing
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Correct and resubmit a rejected filing: 10 days from Service of the rejection notice (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 18(g), (i)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Cure a conditional dismissal or default for a late statement or brief
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Cure a conditional dismissal or default for a late statement or brief: 10 days from Entry of the conditional order (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 18A).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Show cause after conditional dismissal for 90 days’ inactivity
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Show cause after conditional dismissal for 90 days’ inactivity: 20 days from Entry of the conditional order of dismissal (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 18B(2)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Objection to a second Clerk extension
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Objection to a second Clerk extension: 7 days from Filing of the motion to extend (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 20(b)). Each Clerk extension is 30 days.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Opposition to a motion
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Opposition to a motion: 10 days from Service of the motion and memorandum (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 28(b)). Reply 10 days after service of the opposition (R. 28(c)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Memorandum opposing a petition for extraordinary writ / certiorari
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Memorandum opposing a petition for extraordinary writ / certiorari: 20 days from Service of the petition and memorandum (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 13(b)). Reply 10 days after service of the opposition (R. 13(c)). No rule deadline to file the petition itself.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Response to Citation of Supplemental Authority
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Response to Citation of Supplemental Authority: 10 days from Filing of the citation (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 16(e)). No reply allowed.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Petition for reargument
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Petition for reargument: 10 days from Filing of the decision (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 25(a)). Opposition within 10 days after receipt (R. 25(b)). Not extendable by the Clerk.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Automatic stay of execution
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Automatic stay of execution: 20 days from Entry of judgment (Super.R.Civ.P. 62(a)). Or until the appeal time expires. Injunctions and receivership judgments are not stayed unless ordered; afterward a supersedeas bond is needed (R. 62(d)).

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — District Court civil appeal for de novo trial in Superior Court
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. District Court civil appeal for de novo trial in Superior Court: 2 days from Entry of District Court judgment (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-12-10). Excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays; costs including a $50 attorney’s fee paid when the appeal is claimed.

docs.t: Rhode Island appeal deadline — Appeal from a Superior Court magistrate to a Superior Court justice
docs.x: Rhode Island appellate deadline. Appeal from a Superior Court magistrate to a Superior Court justice: 20 days from Entry of the magistrate’s judgment, order, or decree (Super. Ct. R. Prac. 2.9(e)). Transcript must be filed within 60 days of entry or the appeal is dismissed absent good cause (R. Prac. 2.9(g)).

docs.t: South Carolina — Filing alone does not commence the action
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Filing alone does not commence the action: An action is commenced on filing only if the summons and complaint are served within the statute of limitations or, failing that, actually served within 120 days after filing. Serve early when limitations is close. (Rule 3(a), SCRCP)

docs.t: South Carolina — Answers in 30 days, motions on 10 days’ notice, 5 extra days after mail service
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Answers in 30 days, motions on 10 days’ notice, 5 extra days after mail service: The answer is due in 30 days. A written motion and its hearing notice must be served at least 10 days before the hearing. Service by mail adds 5 days in the trial courts, but no days are added for mail in the appellate courts (Rule 263(a), SCACR). (Rules 6(d), 6(e), 12(a), SCRCP; Rule 263(a), SCACR)

docs.t: South Carolina — Every motion needs a good-faith consultation affirmation
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Every motion needs a good-faith consultation affirmation: All motions must affirm that counsel communicated with opposing counsel and tried in good faith to resolve the issue, or certify why consultation would be useless or untimely. The listed exceptions include dispositive and post-trial motions and motions against pro se parties. (Rule 11(a), SCRCP)

docs.t: South Carolina — Discovery caps you will not see in federal court
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Discovery caps you will not see in federal court: General interrogatories beyond the standard set require at least $25,000 in controversy (or declaratory, injunctive, or family court relief) and are capped at 50 including subparts. Requests for admission are capped at 20 per party. Rule 35 exams are available only when more than $100,000 in actual damages is in controversy. (Rules 33(b), 35(a), 36(c), SCRCP)

docs.t: South Carolina — Notice of appeal: serve in 30 days from receipt of written notice of entry, then file within 10 days
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Notice of appeal: serve in 30 days from receipt of written notice of entry, then file within 10 days: In civil cases, the notice of appeal must be served on all respondents within 30 days after receipt of written notice of entry of the order or judgment. Within 10 days after service, file it with the lower court clerk and the appellate clerk, with proof of service, the order, and the $250 fee. A late notice or an unpaid fee means dismissal. No court can extend the notice-of-appeal deadline. (Rules 203(b)(1), 203(d)(1)(B), 203(d)(3), 263(b), SCACR)

docs.t: South Carolina — Post-trial motion deadlines changed in 2026: now 20 days
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Post-trial motion deadlines changed in 2026: now 20 days: An April 30, 2026 order extended the time for JNOV, Rule 52(b), and Rule 59 motions (including 59(e)) from 10 to 20 days. A timely motion stays the appeal time for all parties until receipt of written notice of entry of the order deciding it. Older SC sources and practice guides still say 10 days. The amendment’s effective date is not shown in the collected text, so check it. (Rules 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e), SCRCP (as amended Apr. 30, 2026); Rule 203(b)(1), SCACR)

docs.t: South Carolina — Rule 60(b) has no catch-all ground
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Rule 60(b) has no catch-all ground: South Carolina’s Rule 60(b) omits the federal ’any other reason that justifies relief’ ground. Grounds (1)-(3) (mistake, new evidence, fraud) carry a hard 1-year limit. (Rule 60(b), SCRCP)

docs.t: South Carolina — Settlements between counsel bind only if in the record or signed
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Settlements between counsel bind only if in the record or signed: An agreement between counsel is enforceable only if it is a consent order or signed stipulation entered in the record, made in open court and noted on the record, or reduced to writing and signed by the parties and their counsel. A handshake or an e-mail exchange is not enough. (Rule 43(k), SCRCP)

docs.t: South Carolina — Appeal stays civil judgments automatically (with exceptions)
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Appeal stays civil judgments automatically (with exceptions): Unlike federal practice, serving a notice of appeal in a civil matter automatically stays the order appealed from. Money judgments, injunctions, family court orders regarding a child or support, ejectment orders, and other listed exceptions are not stayed without supersedeas. Apply to the lower court first. (Rule 241(a), (b), (d)(1), SCACR)

docs.t: South Carolina — Rehearing must be actually received in 15 days, and it frames certiorari
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Rehearing must be actually received in 15 days, and it frames certiorari: A petition for rehearing (limit 15 pages) must be actually received by the appellate court within 15 days after the opinion is filed; mailing it is not enough. A Court of Appeals decision cannot be reviewed by the Supreme Court until rehearing has been decided. The certiorari petition may raise only questions raised in the Court of Appeals and in the rehearing petition. (Rules 221(a), 242(c), 242(d)(1), SCACR)

docs.t: South Carolina — Pro hac vice is not a shortcut: local counsel signs and attends, and you cannot e-file
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Pro hac vice is not a shortcut: local counsel signs and attends, and you cannot e-file: Your SC co-counsel must sign every paper and attend every proceeding unless excused. You cannot register for trial-court e-filing. More than six applications in a calendar year bars further pro hac vice appearances. (Rule 404(f), (i), SCACR; SC Electronic Filing Policies and Guidelines § 3(a)(1))

docs.t: South Carolina — Demand letters: no threats of prosecution or bar complaints
docs.x: South Carolina land mine. Demand letters: no threats of prosecution or bar complaints: South Carolina keeps the old Code rule: a lawyer may not threaten criminal or disciplinary charges solely to gain an advantage in a civil matter. (Rule 4.5, RPC, Rule 407, SCACR)

docs.t: South Carolina anti-SLAPP — No anti-SLAPP statute in the South Carolina Code
docs.x: South Carolina anti-SLAPP. No anti-SLAPP statute in the South Carolina Code: South Carolina has no anti-SLAPP law: no special motion to dismiss, no discovery stay, and no fee-shifting tied to speech or petitioning. The suggested cite ’S.C. Code § 15-26-10 et seq.’ does not exist. Title 15 has no Chapter 26 (its chapter list jumps from Chapter 19 to Chapter 27), and the old chapter URL returns 404. Searches of the Code of Laws on scstatehouse.gov (current through the 2026 session) for ’SLAPP’, ’strategic lawsuit’, ’petition the government’, ’exercise of the right of petition’, ’participation in government’, and ’free speech in connection’ found nothing relevant. (S.C. Code tit. 15 chapter index; Code of Laws searches, scstatehouse.gov (Nov. 10, 2026))

docs.t: South Carolina anti-SLAPP — Pending bill only: S. 43 / H. 3305, ’South Carolina Public Expression Protection Act’
docs.x: South Carolina anti-SLAPP. Pending bill only: S. 43 / H. 3305, ’South Carolina Public Expression Protection Act’: S. 43 (2025-2026 session, sponsored by Sen. Campsen, similar to H. 3305) would add Article 7 to Chapter 3 of Title 15. It would create a procedure for civil claims based on a person’s communication in certain circumstances. It was prefiled December 11, 2024 and referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee on January 14, 2025. The bill status page shows no later action. It is not law.
