If it is ever enacted, its scope, deadlines, fee rules, and appeal rights must be read from the ratified act; none are described here. (S. 43, 126th Gen. Assemb. (S.C. 2025-2026), bill status page)

docs.t: South Carolina anti-SLAPP — What a speech defendant can use instead
docs.x: South Carolina anti-SLAPP. What a speech defendant can use instead: Without an anti-SLAPP statute, the tools are an ordinary Rule 12(b)(6) motion (the SC wording is failure ’to state facts sufficient to constitute a cause of action’), summary judgment under Rule 56, Rule 11 sanctions, and the Frivolous Civil Proceedings Sanctions Act. Under the Act, after a verdict or a dismissal by directed verdict, summary judgment, or JNOV, the prevailing party may move for sanctions against a frivolous claim. The test is what a reasonable attorney would believe, proof is by a preponderance, and the person accused gets notice and 30 days to respond. Unlike anti-SLAPP fee shifting, this does not end the case early and does not shift fees automatically. (Rules 11, 12(b)(6), 56, SCRCP; S.C. Code § 15-36-10(A)(4), (C), (D))

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Serve notice of appeal (civil, common pleas, domestic family court, masters, probate)
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Serve notice of appeal (civil, common pleas, domestic family court, masters, probate): 30 days from Receipt of written notice of entry of the order or judgment (Rule 203(b)(1), SCACR). Cannot be extended by any court (Rule 263(b)). Restarts from receipt of written notice of entry of the order deciding a timely Rule 50, 52 or 59 motion.

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — File the served notice of appeal with lower court and appellate clerks
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. File the served notice of appeal with lower court and appellate clerks: 10 days from Service of the notice of appeal (Rule 203(d)(1)(B), SCACR). With proof of service, copy of order, and $250 fee; failure means dismissal (Rule 203(d)(3)).

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Serve and file notice of appeal from an administrative tribunal
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Serve and file notice of appeal from an administrative tribunal: 30 days from Receipt of the decision (Rule 203(b)(6), (d)(2)(B), SCACR). A timely petition for rehearing to the tribunal stays the time.

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Cross-appeal
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Cross-appeal: 5 days from Receipt of appellant’s notice of appeal (Rule 203(c), SCACR). Or the regular Rule 203(b) time, whichever expires later.

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Post-trial motions that stay appeal time (JNOV, 52(b), 59 new trial, 59(e))
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Post-trial motions that stay appeal time (JNOV, 52(b), 59 new trial, 59(e)): 20 days from Jury discharge (jury cases) or receipt of written notice of entry (non-jury and 59(e)) (Rules 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e), SCRCP). Extended from 10 days by the April 30, 2026 amendments; effective date not shown in collected text.

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Order transcript (civil)
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Order transcript (civil): 10 days from Service of notice of appeal (Rule 207(a)(1), SCACR). 30 days in General Sessions and juvenile appeals.

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Appellant’s initial brief
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Appellant’s initial brief: 30 days from Receipt of transcript (or service of notice of appeal if none) (Rule 208(a)(1), SCACR). Missing it produces a clerk’s dismissal order.

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Respondent’s initial brief
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Respondent’s initial brief: 30 days from Service of appellant’s brief (Rule 208(a)(2), SCACR).

docs.t: South Carolina appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Reply brief: 10 days from Service of respondent’s brief (Rule 208(a)(3), SCACR). Optional.
